units.leftText: After the death of Joshua, the Israelites inquired of the LORD, “Who will be the first to go up and fight for us against the Canaanites?”
units.rightText: And it came to pass after the death of Joshua, that the children of Israel asked of Jehovah, saying, Who shall go up for us first against the Canaanites, to fight against them?

units.leftText: “Judah shall go up,” answered the LORD. “Indeed, I have delivered the land into their hands.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said, Judah shall go up: behold, I have delivered the land into his hand.

units.leftText: Then the men of Judah said to their brothers the Simeonites, “Come up with us to our allotted territory, and let us fight against the Canaanites. And we likewise will go with you to your territory.” So the Simeonites went with them.
units.rightText: And Judah said unto Simeon his brother, Come up with me into my lot, that we may fight against the Canaanites; and I likewise will go with thee into thy lot. So Simeon went with him.

units.leftText: When Judah attacked, the LORD delivered the Canaanites and Perizzites into their hands, and they struck down ten thousand men at Bezek.
units.rightText: And Judah went up; and Jehovah delivered the Canaanites and the Perizzites into their hand: and they smote of them in Bezek ten thousand men.

units.leftText: And there they found Adoni-bezek and fought against him, striking down the Canaanites and Perizzites.
units.rightText: And they found Adoni-bezek in Bezek; and they fought against him, and they smote the Canaanites and the Perizzites.

units.leftText: As Adoni-bezek
units.rightText: But Adoni-bezek fled; and they pursued after him, and caught him, and cut off his thumbs and his great toes.

units.leftText: Then Adoni-bezek said, “Seventy kings with their thumbs and big toes cut off have gathered the scraps under my table. As I have done to them, so God has repaid me.” And they brought him to Jerusalem, where he died. The Capture of Jerusalem and Hebron (Joshua 15:13–19|JOS 15:13-19*)
units.rightText: And Adoni-bezek said, Threescore and ten kings, having their thumbs and their great toes cut off, gathered their food under my table: as I have done, so God hath requited me. And they brought him to Jerusalem, and he died there.

units.leftText: Then the men of Judah fought against Jerusalem and captured it. They put the city to the sword and set it on fire.
units.rightText: And the children of Judah fought against Jerusalem, and took it, and smote it with the edge of the sword, and set the city on fire.

units.leftText: Afterward, the men of Judah marched down to fight against the Canaanites living in the hill country, in the Negev, and in the foothills.
units.rightText: And afterward the children of Judah went down to fight against the Canaanites that dwelt in the hill-country, and in the South, and in the lowland.
leftNotes: 1:9 Hebrew Shephelah or lowlands; that is, the western foothills of Judea

units.leftText: Judah also marched against the Canaanites who were living in Hebron (formerly known as Kiriath-arba), and they struck down Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai.
units.rightText: And Judah went against the Canaanites that dwelt in Hebron (now the name of Hebron beforetime was Kiriath-arba); and they smote Sheshai, and Ahiman, and Talmai.

units.leftText: From there they marched against the inhabitants of Debir (formerly known as Kiriath-sepher).
units.rightText: And from thence he went against the inhabitants of Debir. (Now the name of Debir beforetime was Kiriath-sepher.)

units.leftText: And Caleb said, “To the man who strikes down Kiriath-sepher and captures it, I will give my daughter Acsah in marriage.”
units.rightText: And Caleb said, He that smiteth Kiriath-sepher, and taketh it, to him will I give Achsah my daughter to wife.

units.leftText: So Othniel son of Caleb’s younger brother Kenaz captured the city, and Caleb gave his daughter Acsah to him in marriage.
units.rightText: And Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb’s younger brother, took it: and he gave him Achsah his daughter to wife.

units.leftText: One day Acsah came to Othniel and urged him to ask her father for a field. When she got off her donkey, Caleb asked her, “What do you desire?”
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when she came unto him, that she moved him to ask of her father a field: and she alighted from off her ass; and Caleb said unto her, What wouldest thou?
leftNotes: 1:14 Hebrew; LXX and Vulgate and he urged her; see Joshua 15:18|JOS 15:18*.

units.leftText: “Give me a blessing,” she answered. “Since you have given me land in the Negev, give me springs of water as well.” So Caleb gave her both the upper and lower springs.
units.rightText: And she said unto him, Give me a blessing; for that thou hast set me in the land of the South, give me also springs of water. And Caleb gave her the upper springs and the nether springs.

units.leftText: Now the descendants of Moses’ father-in-law, the Kenite, went up with the men of Judah from the City of Palms to the Wilderness of Judah in the Negev near Arad. They went to live among the people.
units.rightText: And the children of the Kenite, Moses’ brother-in-law, went up out of the city of palm-trees with the children of Judah into the wilderness of Judah, which is in the south of Arad; and they went and dwelt with the people.
leftNotes: 1:16 That is, Jericho

units.leftText: Then the men of Judah went with their brothers the Simeonites, attacked the Canaanites living in Zephath, and devoted the city to destruction. So it was called Hormah.
units.rightText: And Judah went with Simeon his brother, and they smote the Canaanites that inhabited Zephath, and utterly destroyed it. And the name of the city was called Hormah.
leftNotes: 1:17 Forms of the Hebrew cherem refer to the giving over of things or persons to the LORD, either by destroying them or by giving them as an offering.
1:17 Hormah means destruction.

units.leftText: And Judah also captured Gaza, Ashkelon, and Ekron — each with its territory.
units.rightText: Also Judah took Gaza with the border thereof, and Ashkelon with the border thereof, and Ekron with the border thereof.
leftNotes: 1:18 Hebrew; LXX But Judah did not capture

units.leftText: The LORD was with Judah, and they took possession of the hill country; but they could not drive out the inhabitants of the plains because they had chariots of iron.
units.rightText: And Jehovah was with Judah; and drove out the inhabitants of the hill-country; for he could not drive out the inhabitants of the valley, because they had chariots of iron.

units.leftText: Just as Moses had promised, Judah gave Hebron to Caleb, who drove out the descendants of the three sons of Anak.
units.rightText: And they gave Hebron unto Caleb, as Moses had spoken: and he drove out thence the three sons of Anak.

units.leftText: The Benjamites, however, failed to drive out the Jebusites living in Jerusalem. So to this day the Jebusites live there among the Benjamites.
units.rightText: And the children of Benjamin did not drive out the Jebusites that inhabited Jerusalem; but the Jebusites dwell with the children of Benjamin in Jerusalem unto this day.

units.leftText: The house of Joseph also attacked Bethel, and the LORD was with them.
units.rightText: And the house of Joseph, they also went up against Beth-el; and Jehovah was with them.

units.leftText: They sent spies to Bethel (formerly known as Luz),
units.rightText: And the house of Joseph sent to spy out Beth-el. (Now the name of the city beforetime was Luz.)

units.leftText: and when the spies saw a man coming out of the city, they said to him, “Please show us how to get into the city, and we will treat you kindly.”
units.rightText: And the watchers saw a man come forth out of the city, and they said unto him, Show us, we pray thee, the entrance into the city, and we will deal kindly with thee.

units.leftText: So the man showed them the entrance to the city, and they put the city to the sword but released that man and all his family.
units.rightText: And he showed them the entrance into the city; and they smote the city with the edge of the sword; but they let the man go and all his family.

units.leftText: And the man went to the land of the Hittites, built a city, and called it Luz, which is its name to this day. The Failure to Complete the Conquest
units.rightText: And the man went into the land of the Hittites, and built a city, and called the name thereof Luz, which is the name thereof unto this day.

units.leftText: At that time Manasseh failed to drive out the inhabitants of Beth-shean, Taanach, Dor, Ibleam, Megiddo, and their villages; for the Canaanites were determined to dwell in that land.
units.rightText: And Manasseh did not drive out the inhabitants of Beth-shean and its towns, nor of Taanach and its towns, nor the inhabitants of Dor and its towns, nor the inhabitants of Ibleam and its towns, nor the inhabitants of Megiddo and its towns; but the Canaanites would dwell in that land.

units.leftText: When Israel became stronger, they pressed the Canaanites into forced labor, but they never drove them out completely.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when Israel was waxed strong, that they put the Canaanites to taskwork, and did not utterly drive them out.

units.leftText: Ephraim also failed to drive out the Canaanites living in Gezer; so the Canaanites continued to dwell among them in Gezer.
units.rightText: And Ephraim drove not out the Canaanites that dwelt in Gezer; but the Canaanites dwelt in Gezer among them.

units.leftText: Zebulun failed to drive out the inhabitants of Kitron and Nahalol; so the Canaanites lived among them and served as forced laborers.
units.rightText: Zebulun drove not out the inhabitants of Kitron, nor the inhabitants of Nahalol; but the Canaanites dwelt among them, and became subject to taskwork.

units.leftText: Asher failed to drive out the inhabitants of Acco, Sidon, Ahlab, Achzib, Helbah, Aphik, and Rehob.
units.rightText: Asher drove not out the inhabitants of Acco, nor the inhabitants of Sidon, nor of Ahlab, nor of Achzib, nor of Helbah, nor of Aphik, nor of Rehob;

units.leftText: So the Asherites lived among the Canaanite inhabitants of the land, because they did not drive them out.
units.rightText: but the Asherites dwelt among the Canaanites, the inhabitants of the land; for they did not drive them out.

units.leftText: Naphtali failed to drive out the inhabitants of Beth-shemesh and Beth-anath. So the Naphtalites also lived among the Canaanite inhabitants of the land, but the inhabitants of Beth-shemesh and Beth-anath served them as forced laborers.
units.rightText: Naphtali drove not out the inhabitants of Beth-shemesh, nor the inhabitants of Beth-anath; but he dwelt among the Canaanites, the inhabitants of the land: nevertheless the inhabitants of Beth-shemesh and of Beth-anath became subject to taskwork.

units.leftText: The Amorites forced the Danites into the hill country and did not allow them to come down into the plain.
units.rightText: And the Amorites forced the children of Dan into the hill-country; for they would not suffer them to come down to the valley;

units.leftText: And the Amorites were determined to dwell in Mount Heres, Aijalon, and Shaalbim. But when the house of Joseph grew in strength, they pressed the Amorites into forced labor.
units.rightText: but the Amorites would dwell in mount Heres, in Aijalon, and in Shaalbim: yet the hand of the house of Joseph prevailed, so that they became subject to taskwork.

units.leftText: And the border of the Amorites extended from the Ascent of Akrabbim to Sela and beyond.
units.rightText: And the border of the Amorites was from the ascent of Akrabbim, from the rock, and upward.
leftNotes: 1:36 Or the Ascent of Scorpions or Scorpion Pass

units.leftText: Now the angel of the LORD went up from Gilgal to Bochim and said, “I brought you up out of Egypt and led you into the land that I had promised to your fathers, and I said, ‘I will never break My covenant with you,
units.rightText: And the angel of Jehovah came up from Gilgal to Bochim. And he said, I made you to go up out of Egypt, and have brought you unto the land which I sware unto your fathers; and I said, I will never break my covenant with you:
leftNotes: 2:1 Or Angel; also in verse 4

units.leftText: and you are not to make a covenant with the people of this land, but you shall tear down their altars.’
units.rightText: and ye shall make no covenant with the inhabitants of this land; ye shall break down their altars. But ye have not hearkened unto my voice: why have ye done this?

units.leftText: So now I tell you that I will not drive out these people before you; they will be thorns in your sides, and their gods will be a snare to you.”
units.rightText: Wherefore I also said, I will not drive them out from before you; but they shall be as thorns in your sides, and their gods shall be a snare unto you.

units.leftText: When the angel of the LORD had spoken these words to all the Israelites, the people lifted up their voices and wept.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when the angel of Jehovah spake these words unto all the children of Israel, that the people lifted up their voice, and wept.

units.leftText: So they called that place Bochim and offered sacrifices there to the LORD. Joshua’s Death and Burial (Joshua 24:29–33|JOS 24:29-33*)
units.rightText: And they called the name of that place Bochim: and they sacrificed there unto Jehovah.
leftNotes: 2:5 Bochim means weepers.

units.leftText: After Joshua had dismissed the people, the Israelites went out to take possession of the land, each to his own inheritance.
units.rightText: Now when Joshua had sent the people away, the children of Israel went every man unto his inheritance to possess the land.

units.leftText: And the people served the LORD throughout the days of Joshua and of the elders who outlived him, who had seen all the great works that the LORD had done for Israel.
units.rightText: And the people served Jehovah all the days of Joshua, and all the days of the elders that outlived Joshua, who had seen all the great work of Jehovah that he had wrought for Israel.

units.leftText: And Joshua son of Nun, the servant of the LORD, died at the age of 110.
units.rightText: And Joshua the son of Nun, the servant of Jehovah, died, being a hundred and ten years old.

units.leftText: They buried him in the land of his inheritance, at Timnath-heres in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash. Israel’s Unfaithfulness (Isaiah 43:22–28|ISA 43:22-28*; Jeremiah 2:23–37|JER 2:23-37*)
units.rightText: And they buried him in the border of his inheritance in Timnath-heres, in the hill-country of Ephraim, on the north of the mountain of Gaash.
leftNotes: 2:9 Timnath-heres is also known as Timnath-serah; see Joshua 19:50|JOS 19:50* and Joshua 24:30.

units.leftText: After that whole generation had also been gathered to their fathers, another generation rose up who did not know the LORD or the works that He had done for Israel.
units.rightText: And also all that generation were gathered unto their fathers: and there arose another generation after them, that knew not Jehovah, nor yet the work which he had wrought for Israel.

units.leftText: And the Israelites did evil in the sight of the LORD and served the Baals.
units.rightText: And the children of Israel did that which was evil in the sight of Jehovah, and served the Baalim;

units.leftText: Thus they forsook the LORD, the God of their fathers, who had brought them out of the land of Egypt, and they followed after various gods of the peoples around them. They bowed down to them and provoked the LORD to anger,
units.rightText: and they forsook Jehovah, the God of their fathers, who brought them out of the land of Egypt, and followed other gods, of the gods of the peoples that were round about them, and bowed themselves down unto them: and they provoked Jehovah to anger.

units.leftText: for they forsook Him and served Baal and the Ashtoreths.
units.rightText: And they forsook Jehovah, and served Baal and the Ashtaroth.

units.leftText: Then the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and He delivered them into the hands of those who plundered them. He sold them into the hands of their enemies all around, whom they were no longer able to resist.
units.rightText: And the anger of Jehovah was kindled against Israel, and he delivered them into the hands of spoilers that despoiled them; and he sold them into the hands of their enemies round about, so that they could not any longer stand before their enemies.
leftNotes: 2:14 Literally of plunderers who plundered them

units.leftText: Wherever Israel marched out, the hand of the LORD was against them to bring calamity, just as He had sworn to them. So they were greatly distressed. Judges Raised Up
units.rightText: Whithersoever they went out, the hand of Jehovah was against them for evil, as Jehovah had spoken, and as Jehovah had sworn unto them: and they were sore distressed.

units.leftText: Then the LORD raised up judges, who saved them from the hands of those who plundered them.
units.rightText: And Jehovah raised up judges, who saved them out of the hand of those that despoiled them.
leftNotes: 2:16 Or governors or leaders; here and throughout the book of Judges

units.leftText: Israel, however, did not listen to their judges. Instead, they prostituted themselves with other gods and bowed down to them. They quickly turned from the way of their fathers, who had walked in obedience to the LORD’s commandments; they did not do as their fathers had done.
units.rightText: And yet they hearkened not unto their judges; for they played the harlot after other gods, and bowed themselves down unto them: they turned aside quickly out of the way wherein their fathers walked, obeying the commandments of Jehovah; but they did not so.

units.leftText: Whenever the LORD raised up a judge for the Israelites, He was with that judge and saved them from the hands of their enemies while the judge was still alive; for the LORD was moved to pity by their groaning under those who oppressed them and afflicted them.
units.rightText: And when Jehovah raised them up judges, then Jehovah was with the judge, and saved them out of the hand of their enemies all the days of the judge: for it repented Jehovah because of their groaning by reason of them that oppressed them and vexed them.

units.leftText: But when the judge died, the Israelites became even more corrupt than their fathers, going after other gods to serve them and bow down to them. They would not give up their evil practices and stubborn ways.
units.rightText: But it came to pass, when the judge was dead, that they turned back, and dealt more corruptly than their fathers, in following other gods to serve them, and to bow down unto them; they ceased not from their doings, nor from their stubborn way.

units.leftText: So the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and He said, “Because this nation has transgressed the covenant I laid down for their fathers and has not heeded My voice,
units.rightText: And the anger of Jehovah was kindled against Israel; and he said, Because this nation have transgressed my covenant which I commanded their fathers, and have not hearkened unto my voice;

units.leftText: I will no longer drive out before them any of the nations Joshua left when he died.
units.rightText: I also will not henceforth drive out any from before them of the nations that Joshua left when he died;

units.leftText: In this way I will test whether Israel will keep the way of the LORD by walking in it as their fathers did.”
units.rightText: that by them I may prove Israel, whether they will keep the way of Jehovah to walk therein, as their fathers did keep it, or not.

units.leftText: That is why the LORD had left those nations in place and had not driven them out immediately by delivering them into the hand of Joshua.
units.rightText: So Jehovah left those nations, without driving them out hastily; neither delivered he them into the hand of Joshua.

units.leftText: These are the nations that the LORD left to test all the Israelites who had not known any of the wars in Canaan,
units.rightText: Now these are the nations which Jehovah left, to prove Israel by them, even as many of Israel as had not known all the wars of Canaan;

units.leftText: if only to teach warfare to the subsequent generations of Israel, especially to those who had not known it formerly:
units.rightText: only that the generations of the children of Israel might know, to teach them war, at the least such as beforetime knew nothing thereof:

units.leftText: the five rulers of the Philistines, all the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites who lived in the mountains of Lebanon from Mount Baal-hermon to Lebo-hamath.
units.rightText: namely, the five lords of the Philistines, and all the Canaanites, and the Sidonians, and the Hivites that dwelt in mount Lebanon, from mount Baal-hermon unto the entrance of Hamath.

units.leftText: These nations were left to test the Israelites, to find out whether they would keep the commandments of the LORD, which He had given their fathers through Moses.
units.rightText: And they were left, to prove Israel by them, to know whether they would hearken unto the commandments of Jehovah, which he commanded their fathers by Moses.

units.leftText: Thus the Israelites continued to live among the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
units.rightText: And the children of Israel dwelt among the Canaanites, the Hittites, and the Amorites, and the Perizzites, and the Hivites, and the Jebusites:

units.leftText: And they took the daughters of these people in marriage, gave their own daughters to their sons, and served their gods. Othniel
units.rightText: and they took their daughters to be their wives, and gave their own daughters to their sons and served their gods.

units.leftText: So the Israelites did evil in the sight of the LORD; they forgot the LORD their God and served the Baals and the Asherahs.
units.rightText: And the children of Israel did that which was evil in the sight of Jehovah, and forgat Jehovah their God, and served the Baalim and the Asheroth.

units.leftText: Then the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and He sold them into the hand of Cushan-rishathaim king of Aram-naharaim, and the Israelites served him eight years.
units.rightText: Therefore the anger of Jehovah was kindled against Israel, and he sold them into the hand of Cushan-rishathaim king of Mesopotamia: and the children of Israel served Cushan-rishathaim eight years.
leftNotes: 3:8 That is, Mesopotamia; Aram-naharaim means Aram of the two rivers, likely the region between the Euphrates and Balih Rivers in northwestern Mesopotamia.

units.leftText: But when the Israelites cried out to the LORD, He raised up Othniel son of Caleb’s younger brother Kenaz as a deliverer to save them.
units.rightText: And when the children of Israel cried unto Jehovah, Jehovah raised up a saviour to the children of Israel, who saved them, even Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb’s younger brother.

units.leftText: The Spirit of the LORD came upon him, and he became Israel’s judge and went out to war. And the LORD delivered Cushan-rishathaim king of Aram into the hand of Othniel, who prevailed against him.
units.rightText: And the Spirit of Jehovah came upon him, and he judged Israel; and he went out to war, and Jehovah delivered Cushan-rishathaim king of Mesopotamia into his hand: and his hand prevailed against Cushan-rishathaim.

units.leftText: So the land had rest for forty years, until Othniel son of Kenaz died. Ehud
units.rightText: And the land had rest forty years. And Othniel the son of Kenaz died.

units.leftText: Once again the Israelites did evil in the sight of the LORD. So He gave Eglon king of Moab power over Israel, because they had done evil in the sight of the LORD.
units.rightText: And the children of Israel again did that which was evil in the sight of Jehovah: and Jehovah strengthened Eglon the king of Moab against Israel, because they had done that which was evil in the sight of Jehovah.

units.leftText: After enlisting the Ammonites and Amalekites to join forces with him, Eglon attacked and defeated Israel, taking possession of the City of Palms.
units.rightText: And he gathered unto him the children of Ammon and Amalek; and he went and smote Israel, and they possessed the city of palm-trees.
leftNotes: 3:13 That is, Jericho

units.leftText: The Israelites served Eglon king of Moab eighteen years.
units.rightText: And the children of Israel served Eglon the king of Moab eighteen years.

units.leftText: And again they cried out to the LORD, and He raised up Ehud son of Gera, a left-handed Benjamite, as their deliverer. So they sent him with tribute to Eglon king of Moab.
units.rightText: But when the children of Israel cried unto Jehovah, Jehovah raised them up a saviour, Ehud the son of Gera, the Benjamite, a man left-handed. And the children of Israel sent tribute by him unto Eglon the king of Moab.

units.leftText: Now Ehud had made for himself a double-edged sword a cubit long. He strapped it to his right thigh under his cloak
units.rightText: And Ehud made him a sword which had two edges, a cubit in length; and he girded it under his raiment upon his right thigh.
leftNotes: 3:16 A cubit is approximately 18 inches or 45.7 centimeters.

units.leftText: and brought the tribute to Eglon king of Moab, who was an obese man.
units.rightText: And he offered the tribute unto Eglon king of Moab: now Eglon was a very fat man.

units.leftText: After Ehud had finished presenting the tribute, he ushered out those who had carried it.
units.rightText: And when he had made an end of offering the tribute, he sent away the people that bare the tribute.

units.leftText: But upon reaching the idols near Gilgal, he himself turned back and said, “I have a secret message for you, O king.” “Silence,” said the king, and all his attendants left him.
units.rightText: But he himself turned back from the quarries that were by Gilgal, and said, I have a secret errand unto thee, O king. And he said, Keep silence. And all that stood by him went out from him.

units.leftText: Then Ehud approached him while he was sitting alone in the coolness of his upper room. “I have a word from God for you,” Ehud said, and the king rose from his seat.
units.rightText: And Ehud came unto him; and he was sitting by himself alone in the cool upper room. And Ehud said, I have a message from God unto thee. And he arose out of his seat.

units.leftText: And Ehud reached with his left hand, pulled the sword from his right thigh, and plunged it into Eglon’s belly.
units.rightText: And Ehud put forth his left hand, and took the sword from his right thigh, and thrust it into his body:

units.leftText: Even the handle sank in after the blade, and Eglon’s fat closed in over it, so that Ehud did not withdraw the sword from his belly. And Eglon’s bowels emptied.
units.rightText: and the haft also went in after the blade; and the fat closed upon the blade, for he drew not the sword out of his body; and it came out behind.

units.leftText: Then Ehud went out through the porch, closing and locking the doors of the upper room behind him.
units.rightText: Then Ehud went forth into the porch, and shut the doors of the upper room upon him, and locked them.

units.leftText: After Ehud was gone, Eglon’s servants came in and found the doors of the upper room locked. “He must be relieving himself in the cool room,” they said.
units.rightText: Now when he was gone out, his servants came; and they saw, and, behold, the doors of the upper room were locked; and they said, Surely he is covering his feet in the upper chamber.

units.leftText: So they waited until they became worried and saw that he had still not opened the doors of the upper room. Then they took the key and opened the doors— and there was their lord lying dead on the floor.
units.rightText: And they tarried till they were ashamed; and, behold, he opened not the doors of the upper room: therefore they took the key, and opened them; and, behold, their lord was fallen down dead on the earth.

units.leftText: Ehud, however, had escaped while the servants waited. He passed by the idols and escaped to Seirah.
units.rightText: And Ehud escaped while they tarried, and passed beyond the quarries, and escaped unto Seirah.

units.leftText: On arriving in Seirah, he blew the ram’s horn throughout the hill country of Ephraim. The Israelites came down with him from the hills, and he became their leader.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when he was come, that he blew a trumpet in the hill-country of Ephraim; and the children of Israel went down with him from the hill-country, and he before them.

units.leftText: “Follow me,” he told them, “for the LORD has delivered your enemies the Moabites into your hand.”
units.rightText: And he said unto them, Follow after me; for Jehovah hath delivered your enemies the Moabites into your hand. And they went down after him, and took the fords of the Jordan against the Moabites, and suffered not a man to pass over.

units.leftText: At that time they struck down about ten thousand Moabites, all robust and valiant men. Not one of them escaped.
units.rightText: And they smote of Moab at that time about ten thousand men, every lusty man, and every man of valor; and there escaped not a man.

units.leftText: So Moab was subdued under the hand of Israel that day, and the land had rest for eighty years. Shamgar
units.rightText: So Moab was subdued that day under the hand of Israel. And the land had rest fourscore years.

units.leftText: After Ehud came Shamgar son of Anath. And he too saved Israel, striking down six hundred Philistines with an oxgoad.
units.rightText: And after him was Shamgar the son of Anath, who smote of the Philistines six hundred men with an ox-goad: and he also saved Israel.

units.leftText: After Ehud died, the Israelites again did evil in the sight of the LORD.
units.rightText: And the children of Israel again did that which was evil in the sight of Jehovah, when Ehud was dead.

units.leftText: So the LORD sold them into the hand of Jabin king of Canaan, who reigned in Hazor. The commander of his forces was Sisera, who lived in Harosheth-hagoyim.
units.rightText: And Jehovah sold them into the hand of Jabin king of Canaan, that reigned in Hazor; the captain of whose host was Sisera, who dwelt in Harosheth of the Gentiles.

units.leftText: Then the Israelites cried out to the LORD, because Jabin had nine hundred chariots of iron, and he had harshly oppressed the Israelites for twenty years.
units.rightText: And the children of Israel cried unto Jehovah: for he had nine hundred chariots of iron; and twenty years he mightily oppressed the children of Israel.

units.leftText: Now Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lappidoth, was judging Israel at that time.
units.rightText: Now Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lappidoth, she judged Israel at that time.

units.leftText: And she would sit under the Palm of Deborah between Ramah and Bethel in the hill country of Ephraim, where the Israelites would go up to her for judgment.
units.rightText: And she dwelt under the palm-tree of Deborah between Ramah and Beth-el in the hill-country of Ephraim: and the children of Israel came up to her for judgment.

units.leftText: She summoned Barak son of Abinoam from Kedesh in Naphtali and said to him, “Surely the LORD, the God of Israel, is commanding you: ‘Go and march to Mount Tabor, taking with you ten thousand men of Naphtali and Zebulun.
units.rightText: And she sent and called Barak the son of Abinoam out of Kedesh-naphtali, and said unto him, Hath not Jehovah, the God of Israel, commanded, saying, Go and draw unto mount Tabor, and take with thee ten thousand men of the children of Naphtali and of the children of Zebulun?

units.leftText: And I will draw out Sisera the commander of Jabin’s army, his chariots, and his troops to the River Kishon, and I will deliver him into your hand.’”
units.rightText: And I will draw unto thee, to the river Kishon, Sisera, the captain of Jabin’s army, with his chariots and his multitude; and I will deliver him into thy hand.

units.leftText: Barak said to her, “If you will go with me, I will go; but if you will not go with me, I will not go.”
units.rightText: And Barak said unto her, If thou wilt go with me, then I will go; but if thou wilt not go with me, I will not go.

units.leftText: “I will certainly go with you,” Deborah replied, “but the road you are taking will bring you no honor, because the LORD will be selling Sisera into the hand of a woman.” So Deborah got up and went with Barak to Kedesh,
units.rightText: And she said, I will surely go with thee: notwithstanding, the journey that thou takest shall not be for thine honor; for Jehovah will sell Sisera into the hand of a woman. And Deborah arose, and went with Barak to Kedesh.

units.leftText: where he summoned Zebulun and Naphtali. Ten thousand men followed him, and Deborah also went with him.
units.rightText: And Barak called Zebulun and Naphtali together to Kedesh; and there went up ten thousand men at his feet: and Deborah went up with him.

units.leftText: Now Heber the Kenite had moved away from the Kenites, the descendants of Hobab the father-in-law of Moses, and had pitched his tent by the great tree of Zaanannim, which was near Kedesh.
units.rightText: Now Heber the Kenite had separated himself from the Kenites, even from the children of Hobab the brother-in-law of Moses, and had pitched his tent as far as the oak in Zaanannim, which is by Kedesh.
leftNotes: 4:11 Or brother-in-law

units.leftText: When Sisera was told that Barak son of Abinoam had gone up Mount Tabor,
units.rightText: And they told Sisera that Barak the son of Abinoam was gone up to mount Tabor.

units.leftText: he summoned all nine hundred of his iron chariots and all the men with him, from Harosheth-hagoyim to the River Kishon.
units.rightText: And Sisera gathered together all his chariots, even nine hundred chariots of iron, and all the people that were with him, from Harosheth of the Gentiles, unto the river Kishon.

units.leftText: Then Deborah said to Barak, “Arise, for this is the day that the LORD has delivered Sisera into your hand. Has not the LORD gone before you?”
units.rightText: And Deborah said unto Barak, Up; for this is the day in which Jehovah hath delivered Sisera into thy hand; is not Jehovah gone out before thee? So Barak went down from mount Tabor, and ten thousand men after him.

units.leftText: And in front of him the LORD routed with the sword Sisera, all his charioteers, and all his army. Sisera abandoned his chariot and fled on foot.
units.rightText: And Jehovah discomfited Sisera, and all his chariots, and all his host, with the edge of the sword before Barak; and Sisera alighted from his chariot, and fled away on his feet.

units.leftText: Then Barak pursued the chariots and army as far as Harosheth-hagoyim, and the whole army of Sisera fell by the sword; not a single man was left. Jael Kills Sisera
units.rightText: But Barak pursued after the chariots, and after the host, unto Harosheth of the Gentiles: and all the host of Sisera fell by the edge of the sword; there was not a man left.

units.leftText: Meanwhile, Sisera had fled on foot to the tent of Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite, because there was peace between Jabin king of Hazor and the house of Heber the Kenite.
units.rightText: Howbeit Sisera fled away on his feet to the tent of Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite; for there was peace between Jabin the king of Hazor and the house of Heber the Kenite.

units.leftText: Jael went out to greet Sisera and said to him, “Come in, my lord. Come in with me. Do not be afraid.” So he entered her tent, and she covered him with a blanket.
units.rightText: And Jael went out to meet Sisera, and said unto him, Turn in, my lord, turn in to me; fear not. And he turned in unto her into the tent, and she covered him with a rug.

units.leftText: Sisera said to her, “Please give me a little water to drink, for I am thirsty.” So she opened a container of milk, gave him a drink, and covered him again.
units.rightText: And he said unto her, Give me, I pray thee, a little water to drink; for I am thirsty. And she opened a bottle of milk, and gave him drink, and covered him.

units.leftText: “Stand at the entrance to the tent,” he said, “and if anyone comes and asks you, ‘Is there a man here?’ say, ‘No.’”
units.rightText: And he said unto her, Stand in the door of the tent, and it shall be, when any man doth come and inquire of thee, and say, Is there any man here? that thou shalt say, No.

units.leftText: But as he lay sleeping from exhaustion, Heber’s wife Jael took a tent peg, grabbed a hammer, and went silently to Sisera. She drove the peg through his temple and into the ground, and he died.
units.rightText: Then Jael Heber’s wife took a tent-pin, and took a hammer in her hand, and went softly unto him, and smote the pin into his temples, and it pierced through into the ground; for he was in a deep sleep; so he swooned and died.

units.leftText: When Barak arrived in pursuit of Sisera, Jael went out to greet him and said to him, “Come, and I will show you the man you are seeking.” So he went in with her, and there lay Sisera dead, with a tent peg through his temple.
units.rightText: And, behold, as Barak pursued Sisera, Jael came out to meet him, and said unto him, Come, and I will show thee the man whom thou seekest. And he came unto her; and, behold, Sisera lay dead, and the tent-pin was in his temples.

units.leftText: On that day God subdued Jabin king of Canaan before the Israelites.
units.rightText: So God subdued on that day Jabin the king of Canaan before the children of Israel.

units.leftText: And the hand of the Israelites grew stronger and stronger against Jabin king of Canaan until they destroyed him.
units.rightText: And the hand of the children of Israel prevailed more and more against Jabin the king of Canaan, until they had destroyed Jabin king of Canaan.

units.leftText: On that day Deborah and Barak son of Abinoam sang this song:
units.rightText: Then sang Deborah and Barak the son of Abinoam on that day, saying,

units.leftText: “When the princes take the lead in Israel, when the people volunteer, bless the LORD.
units.rightText: For that the leaders took the lead in Israel, For that the people offered themselves willingly, Bless ye Jehovah.

units.leftText: Listen, O kings! Give ear, O princes! I will sing to the LORD; I will sing praise to the LORD, the God of Israel.
units.rightText: Hear, O ye kings; give ear, O ye princes; I, even I, will sing unto Jehovah; I will sing praise to Jehovah, the God of Israel.

units.leftText: O LORD, when You went out from Seir, when You marched from the land of Edom, the earth trembled, the heavens poured out rain, and the clouds poured down water.
units.rightText: Jehovah, when thou wentest forth out of Seir, When thou marchedst out of the field of Edom, The earth trembled, the heavens also dropped, Yea, the clouds dropped water.

units.leftText: The mountains quaked before the LORD, the One of Sinai, before the LORD, the God of Israel.
units.rightText: The mountains quaked at the presence of Jehovah, Even yon Sinai at the presence of Jehovah, the God of Israel.

units.leftText: In the days of Shamgar son of Anath, in the days of Jael, the highways were deserted and the travelers took the byways.
units.rightText: In the days of Shamgar the son of Anath, In the days of Jael, the highways were unoccupied, And the travellers walked through byways.

units.leftText: Life in the villages ceased; it ended in Israel, until I, Deborah, arose, a mother in Israel.
units.rightText: The rulers ceased in Israel, they ceased, Until that I Deborah arose, That I arose a mother in Israel.

units.leftText: When they chose new gods, then war came to their gates. Not a shield or spear was found among forty thousand in Israel.
units.rightText: They chose new gods; Then was war in the gates: Was there a shield or spear seen Among forty thousand in Israel?

units.leftText: My heart is with the princes of Israel, with the volunteers among the people. Bless the LORD!
units.rightText: My heart is toward the governors of Israel, That offered themselves willingly among the people: Bless ye Jehovah.

units.leftText: You who ride white donkeys, who sit on saddle blankets, and you who travel the road,
units.rightText: Tell of it, ye that ride on white asses, Ye that sit on rich carpets, And ye that walk by the way.

units.leftText: the voices of the singers at the watering places. There they shall recount the righteous acts of the LORD, the righteous deeds of His villagers in Israel. Then the people of the LORD went down to the gates:
units.rightText: Far from the noise of archers, in the places of drawing water, There shall they rehearse the righteous acts of Jehovah, Even the righteous acts of his rule in Israel. Then the people of Jehovah went down to the gates.
leftNotes: 5:11 Or archers or those who divide the sheep
5:11 Or warriors

units.leftText: ‘Awake, awake, O Deborah! Awake, awake, sing a song! Arise, O Barak, and take hold of your captives, O son of Abinoam!’
units.rightText: Awake, awake, Deborah; Awake, awake, utter a song: Arise, Barak, and lead away thy captives, thou son of Abinoam.

units.leftText: Then the survivors came down to the nobles; the people of the LORD came down to me against the mighty.
units.rightText: Then came down a remnant of the nobles and the people; Jehovah came down for me against the mighty.

units.leftText: Some came from Ephraim, with their roots in Amalek; Benjamin came with your people after you. The commanders came down from Machir, the bearers of the marshal’s staff from Zebulun.
units.rightText: Out of Ephraim came down they whose root is in Amalek; After thee, Benjamin, among thy peoples; Out of Machir came down governors, And out of Zebulun they that handle the marshal’s staff.

units.leftText: The princes of Issachar were with Deborah, and Issachar was with Barak, rushing into the valley at his heels. In the clans of Reuben there was great indecision.
units.rightText: And the princes of Issachar were with Deborah; As was Issachar, so was Barak; Into the valley they rushed forth at his feet. By the watercourses of Reuben There were great resolves of heart.
leftNotes: 5:15 Or much searching of heart; also in verse 16

units.leftText: Why did you sit among the sheepfolds to hear the whistling for the flocks? In the clans of Reuben there was great indecision.
units.rightText: Why sattest thou among the sheepfolds, To hear the pipings for the flocks? At the watercourses of Reuben There were great searchings of heart.

units.leftText: Gilead remained beyond the Jordan. Dan, why did you linger by the ships? Asher stayed at the coast and remained in his harbors.
units.rightText: Gilead abode beyond the Jordan: And Dan, why did he remain in ships? Asher sat still at the haven of the sea, And abode by his creeks.

units.leftText: Zebulun was a people who risked their lives; Naphtali, too, on the heights of the battlefield.
units.rightText: Zebulun was a people that jeoparded their lives unto the death, And Naphtali, upon the high places of the field.

units.leftText: Kings came and fought; then the kings of Canaan fought at Taanach by the waters of Megiddo, but they took no plunder of silver.
units.rightText: The kings came and fought; Then fought the kings of Canaan, In Taanach by the waters of Megiddo: They took no gain of money.

units.leftText: From the heavens the stars fought; from their courses they fought against Sisera.
units.rightText: From heaven fought the stars, From their courses they fought against Sisera.

units.leftText: The River Kishon swept them away, the ancient river, the River Kishon. March on, O my soul, in strength!
units.rightText: The river Kishon swept them away, That ancient river, the river Kishon. O my soul, march on with strength.

units.leftText: Then the hooves of horses thundered— the mad galloping of his stallions.
units.rightText: Then did the horsehoofs stamp By reason of the prancings, the prancings of their strong ones.

units.leftText: ‘Curse Meroz,’ says the angel of the LORD. ‘Bitterly curse her inhabitants; for they did not come to help the LORD, to help the LORD against the mighty.’
units.rightText: Curse ye Meroz, said the angel of Jehovah. Curse ye bitterly the inhabitants thereof, Because they came not to the help of Jehovah, To the help of Jehovah against the mighty.

units.leftText: Most blessed among women is Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite, most blessed of tent-dwelling women.
units.rightText: Blessed above women shall Jael be, The wife of Heber the Kenite; Blessed shall she be above women in the tent.

units.leftText: He asked for water, and she gave him milk. In a magnificent bowl she brought him curds.
units.rightText: He asked water, and she gave him milk; She brought him butter in a lordly dish.

units.leftText: She reached for the tent peg, her right hand for the workman’s hammer. She struck Sisera and crushed his skull; she shattered and pierced his temple.
units.rightText: She put her hand to the tent-pin, And her right hand to the workmen’s hammer; And with the hammer she smote Sisera, she smote through his head; Yea, she pierced and struck through his temples.

units.leftText: At her feet he collapsed, he fell, there he lay still; at her feet he collapsed, he fell; where he collapsed, there he fell dead.
units.rightText: At her feet he bowed, he fell, he lay; At her feet he bowed, he fell: Where he bowed, there he fell down dead.

units.leftText: Sisera’s mother looked through the window; she peered through the lattice and lamented: ‘Why is his chariot so long in coming? What has delayed the clatter of his chariots?’
units.rightText: Through the window she looked forth, and cried, The mother of Sisera cried through the lattice, Why is his chariot so long in coming? Why tarry the wheels of his chariots?

units.leftText: Her wisest ladies answer; indeed she keeps telling herself,
units.rightText: Her wise ladies answered her, Yea, she returned answer to herself,

units.leftText: ‘Are they not finding and dividing the spoil— a girl or two for each warrior, a plunder of dyed garments for Sisera, the spoil of embroidered garments for the neck of the looter?’
units.rightText: Have they not found, have they not divided the spoil? A damsel, two damsels to every man; To Sisera a spoil of dyed garments, A spoil of dyed garments embroidered, Of dyed garments embroidered on both sides, on the necks of the spoil?

units.leftText: So may all Your enemies perish, O LORD! But may those who love You shine like the sun at its brightest.” And the land had rest for forty years.
units.rightText: So let all thine enemies perish, O Jehovah: But let them that love him be as the sun when he goeth forth in his might. And the land had rest forty years.

units.leftText: Again the Israelites did evil in the sight of the LORD; so He delivered them into the hand of Midian for seven years,
units.rightText: And the children of Israel did that which was evil in the sight of Jehovah: and Jehovah delivered them into the hand of Midian seven years.

units.leftText: and the hand of Midian prevailed against Israel. Because of the Midianites, the Israelites prepared shelters for themselves in the mountains, caves, and strongholds.
units.rightText: And the hand of Midian prevailed against Israel; and because of Midian the children of Israel made them the dens which are in the mountains, and the caves, and the strongholds.

units.leftText: Whenever the Israelites planted their crops, the Midianites, Amalekites, and other people of the east would come up and invade them,
units.rightText: And so it was, when Israel had sown, that the Midianites came up, and the Amalekites, and the children of the east; they came up against them;

units.leftText: encamping against them as far as Gaza and destroying the produce of the land. They left Israel with no sustenance, neither sheep nor oxen nor donkeys.
units.rightText: and they encamped against them, and destroyed the increase of the earth, till thou come unto Gaza, and left no sustenance in Israel, neither sheep, nor ox, nor ass.

units.leftText: For the Midianites came with their livestock and their tents like a great swarm of locusts. They and their camels were innumerable, and they entered the land to ravage it.
units.rightText: For they came up with their cattle and their tents; they came in as locusts for multitude; both they and their camels were without number: and they came into the land to destroy it.

units.leftText: Israel was greatly impoverished by Midian, and the Israelites cried out to the LORD.
units.rightText: And Israel was brought very low because of Midian; and the children of Israel cried unto Jehovah.

units.leftText: Now when the Israelites cried out to the LORD because of Midian,
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when the children of Israel cried unto Jehovah because of Midian,

units.leftText: He sent them a prophet, who told them, “This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: I brought you up out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
units.rightText: that Jehovah sent a prophet unto the children of Israel: and he said unto them, Thus saith Jehovah, the God of Israel, I brought you up from Egypt, and brought you forth out of the house of bondage;

units.leftText: I delivered you out of the hands of Egypt and all your oppressors. I drove them out before you and gave you their land.
units.rightText: and I delivered you out of the hand of the Egyptians, and out of the hand of all that oppressed you, and drove them out from before you, and gave you their land;

units.leftText: And I said to you: ‘I am the LORD your God. You must not fear the gods of the Amorites, in whose land you dwell.’ But you did not obey Me.” The Call of Gideon
units.rightText: and I said unto you, I am Jehovah your God; ye shall not fear the gods of the Amorites, in whose land ye dwell. But ye have not hearkened unto my voice.
leftNotes: 6:10 Or worship

units.leftText: Then the angel of the LORD came and sat down under the oak in Ophrah that belonged to Joash the Abiezrite, where his son Gideon was threshing wheat in a winepress to hide it from the Midianites.
units.rightText: And the angel of Jehovah came, and sat under the oak which was in Ophrah, that pertained unto Joash the Abiezrite: and his son Gideon was beating out wheat in the winepress, to hide it from the Midianites.
leftNotes: 6:11 Or Angel; also in verses 12, 20, 21, and 22; corresponding pronouns may also be capitalized.
6:11 Or terebinth or great tree; also in verse 19

units.leftText: And the angel of the LORD appeared to Gideon and said, “The LORD is with you, O mighty man of valor.”
units.rightText: And the angel of Jehovah appeared unto him, and said unto him, Jehovah is with thee, thou mighty man of valor.

units.leftText: “Please, my Lord,” Gideon replied, “if the LORD is with us, why has all this happened to us? And where are all His wonders of which our fathers told us, saying, ‘Has not the LORD brought us up out of Egypt?’ But now the LORD has forsaken us and delivered us into the hand of Midian.”
units.rightText: And Gideon said unto him, Oh, my lord, if Jehovah is with us, why then is all this befallen us? and where are all his wondrous works which our fathers told us of, saying, Did not Jehovah bring us up from Egypt? but now Jehovah hath cast us off, and delivered us into the hand of Midian.

units.leftText: The LORD turned to him and said, “Go in the strength you have and save Israel from the hand of Midian. Am I not sending you?”
units.rightText: And Jehovah looked upon him, and said, Go in this thy might, and save Israel from the hand of Midian: have not I sent thee?
leftNotes: 6:14 LXX The angel of the LORD or The Angel of the LORD; also in verse 16

units.leftText: “Please, my Lord,” Gideon replied, “how can I save Israel? Indeed, my clan is the weakest in Manasseh, and I am the youngest in my father’s house.”
units.rightText: And he said unto him, Oh, Lord, wherewith shall I save Israel? behold, my family is the poorest in Manasseh, and I am the least in my father’s house.

units.leftText: “Surely I will be with you,” the LORD replied, “and you will strike down all the Midianites as one man.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto him, Surely I will be with thee, and thou shalt smite the Midianites as one man.

units.leftText: Gideon answered, “If I have found favor in Your sight, give me a sign that it is You speaking with me.
units.rightText: And he said unto him, If now I have found favor in thy sight, then show me a sign that it is thou that talkest with me.

units.leftText: Please do not depart from this place until I return to You. Let me bring my offering and set it before You.” And the LORD said, “I will stay until you return.”
units.rightText: Depart not hence, I pray thee, until I come unto thee, and bring forth my present, and lay it before thee. And he said, I will tarry until thou come again.

units.leftText: So Gideon went in and prepared a young goat and unleavened bread and an ephah of flour. He placed the meat in a basket and the broth in a pot and brought them out to present to Him under the oak.
units.rightText: And Gideon went in, and made ready a kid, and unleavened cakes of an ephah of meal: the flesh he put in a basket, and he put the broth in a pot, and brought it out unto him under the oak, and presented it.
leftNotes: 6:19 An ephah is approximately 20 dry quarts or 22 liters (probably about 25.5 pounds or 11.6 kilograms of flour).

units.leftText: And the angel of God said to him, “Take the meat and the unleavened bread, lay them on this rock, and pour out the broth.” And Gideon did so.
units.rightText: And the angel of God said unto him, Take the flesh and the unleavened cakes, and lay them upon this rock, and pour out the broth. And he did so.

units.leftText: Then the angel of the LORD extended the tip of the staff that was in his hand and touched the meat and the unleavened bread. And fire flared from the rock and consumed the meat and the unleavened bread. Then the angel of the LORD vanished from his sight.
units.rightText: Then the angel of Jehovah put forth the end of the staff that was in his hand, and touched the flesh and the unleavened cakes; and there went up fire out of the rock, and consumed the flesh and the unleavened cakes; and the angel of Jehovah departed out of his sight.

units.leftText: When Gideon realized that it was the angel of the LORD, he said, “Oh no, Lord GOD! I have seen the angel of the LORD face to face!”
units.rightText: And Gideon saw that he was the angel of Jehovah; and Gideon said, Alas, O Lord Jehovah! forasmuch as I have seen the angel of Jehovah face to face.

units.leftText: But the LORD said to him, “Peace be with you. Do not be afraid, for you will not die.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto him, Peace be unto thee; fear not: thou shalt not die.

units.leftText: So Gideon built an altar to the LORD there and called it The LORD Is Peace. To this day it stands in Ophrah of the Abiezrites. Gideon Destroys Baal’s Altar
units.rightText: Then Gideon built an altar there unto Jehovah, and called it Jehovah-shalom: unto this day it is yet in Ophrah of the Abiezrites.
leftNotes: 6:24 Hebrew YHWH Shalom

units.leftText: On that very night the LORD said to Gideon, “Take your father’s young bull and a second bull seven years old, tear down your father’s altar to Baal, and cut down the Asherah pole beside it.
units.rightText: And it came to pass the same night, that Jehovah said unto him, Take thy father’s bullock, even the second bullock seven years old, and throw down the altar of Baal that thy father hath, and cut down the Asherah that is by it;

units.leftText: Then build a proper altar to the LORD your God on the top of this stronghold. And with the wood of the Asherah pole you cut down, take the second bull and offer it as a burnt offering.”
units.rightText: and build an altar unto Jehovah thy God upon the top of this stronghold, in the orderly manner, and take the second bullock, and offer a burnt-offering with the wood of the Asherah which thou shalt cut down.

units.leftText: So Gideon took ten of his servants and did as the LORD had told him. But because he was too afraid of his father’s household and the men of the city, he did it by night rather than in the daytime.
units.rightText: Then Gideon took ten men of his servants, and did as Jehovah had spoken unto him: and it came to pass, because he feared his father’s household and the men of the city, so that he could not do it by day, that he did it by night.

units.leftText: When the men of the city got up in the morning, there was Baal’s altar torn down, with the Asherah pole cut down beside it and the second bull offered up on the newly built altar.
units.rightText: And when the men of the city arose early in the morning, behold, the altar of Baal was broken down, and the Asherah was cut down that was by it, and the second bullock was offered upon the altar that was built.

units.leftText: “Who did this?” they said to one another. And after they had investigated thoroughly, they were told, “Gideon son of Joash did it.”
units.rightText: And they said one to another, Who hath done this thing? And when they inquired and asked, they said, Gideon the son of Joash hath done this thing.

units.leftText: Then the men of the city said to Joash, “Bring out your son. He must die, because he has torn down Baal’s altar and cut down the Asherah pole beside it.”
units.rightText: Then the men of the city said unto Joash, Bring out thy son, that he may die, because he hath broken down the altar of Baal, and because he hath cut down the Asherah that was by it.

units.leftText: But Joash said to all who stood against him, “Are you contending for Baal? Are you trying to save him? Whoever pleads his case will be put to death by morning! If Baal is a god, let him contend for himself with the one who has torn down his altar.”
units.rightText: And Joash said unto all that stood against him, Will ye contend for Baal? or will ye save him? he that will contend for him, let him be put to death whilst it is yet morning: if he be a god, let him contend for himself, because one hath broken down his altar.

units.leftText: So on that day Gideon was called Jerubbaal, that is to say, “Let Baal contend with him,” because he had torn down Baal’s altar. The Sign of the Fleece
units.rightText: Therefore on that day he called him Jerubbaal, saying, Let Baal contend against him, because he hath broken down his altar.
leftNotes: 6:32 Jerubbaal probably means let Baal contend.

units.leftText: Then all the Midianites, Amalekites, and other people of the east gathered together, crossed over the Jordan, and camped in the Valley of Jezreel.
units.rightText: Then all the Midianites and the Amalekites and the children of the east assembled themselves together; and they passed over, and encamped in the valley of Jezreel.

units.leftText: So the Spirit of the LORD came upon Gideon, who blew the ram’s horn and rallied the Abiezrites behind him.
units.rightText: But the Spirit of Jehovah came upon Gideon; and he blew a trumpet; and Abiezer was gathered together after him.

units.leftText: Calling them to arms, Gideon sent messengers throughout Manasseh, as well as Asher, Zebulun, and Naphtali, so that they came up to meet him.
units.rightText: And he sent messengers throughout all Manasseh; and they also were gathered together after him: and he sent messengers unto Asher, and unto Zebulun, and unto Naphtali; and they came up to meet them.

units.leftText: Then Gideon said to God, “If You are going to save Israel by my hand, as You have said,
units.rightText: And Gideon said unto God, If thou wilt save Israel by my hand, as thou hast spoken,

units.leftText: then behold, I will place a fleece of wool on the threshing floor. If there is dew only on the fleece and all the ground is dry, then I will know that You are going to save Israel by my hand, as You have said.”
units.rightText: behold, I will put a fleece of wool on the threshing-floor; if there be dew on the fleece only, and it be dry upon all the ground, then shall I know that thou wilt save Israel by my hand, as thou hast spoken.

units.leftText: And that is what happened. When Gideon arose the next morning, he squeezed the fleece and wrung out the dew — a bowlful of water.
units.rightText: And it was so; for he rose up early on the morrow, and pressed the fleece together, and wrung the dew out of the fleece, a bowlful of water.

units.leftText: Then Gideon said to God, “Do not be angry with me; let me speak one more time. Please allow me one more test with the fleece. This time let it be dry, and the ground covered with dew.”
units.rightText: And Gideon said unto God, Let not thine anger be kindled against me, and I will speak but this once: let me make trial, I pray thee, but this once with the fleece; let it now be dry only upon the fleece, and upon all the ground let there be dew.

units.leftText: And that night God did so. Only the fleece was dry, and dew covered the ground.
units.rightText: And God did so that night: for it was dry upon the fleece only, and there was dew on all the ground.

units.leftText: Early in the morning Jerubbaal (that is, Gideon) and all the men with him camped beside the spring of Harod. And the camp of Midian was north of them in the valley near the hill of Moreh.
units.rightText: Then Jerubbaal, who is Gideon, and all the people that were with him, rose up early, and encamped beside the spring of Harod: and the camp of Midian was on the north side of them, by the hill of Moreh, in the valley.
leftNotes: 7:1 Jerubbaal is another name for Gideon and probably means let Baal contend; see Judges 6:32|JDG 6:32*.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Gideon, “You have too many men for Me to deliver Midian into their hands, lest Israel glorify themselves over Me, saying, ‘My own hand has saved me.’
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Gideon, The people that are with thee are too many for me to give the Midianites into their hand, lest Israel vaunt themselves against me, saying, Mine own hand hath saved me.

units.leftText: Now, therefore, proclaim in the hearing of the men: ‘Whoever is fearful and trembling may turn back and leave Mount Gilead.’” So twenty-two thousand of them turned back, but ten thousand remained.
units.rightText: Now therefore proclaim in the ears of the people, saying, Whosoever is fearful and trembling, let him return and depart from mount Gilead. And there returned of the people twenty and two thousand; and there remained ten thousand.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Gideon, “There are still too many men. Take them down to the water, and I will sift them for you there. If I say to you, ‘This one shall go with you,’ he shall go. But if I say, ‘This one shall not go with you,’ he shall not go.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Gideon, The people are yet too many; bring them down unto the water, and I will try them for thee there: and it shall be, that of whom I say unto thee, This shall go with thee, the same shall go with thee; and of whomsoever I say unto thee, This shall not go with thee, the same shall not go.

units.leftText: So Gideon brought the men down to the water, and the LORD said to him, “Separate those who lap the water with their tongues like a dog from those who kneel to drink.”
units.rightText: So he brought down the people unto the water: and Jehovah said unto Gideon, Every one that lappeth of the water with his tongue, as a dog lappeth, him shalt thou set by himself; likewise every one that boweth down upon his knees to drink.

units.leftText: And the number of those who lapped the water with their hands to their mouths was three hundred men; all the others knelt to drink.
units.rightText: And the number of them that lapped, putting their hand to their mouth, was three hundred men: but all the rest of the people bowed down upon their knees to drink water.

units.leftText: Then the LORD said to Gideon, “With the three hundred men who lapped the water I will save you and deliver the Midianites into your hand. But all the others are to go home.”
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto Gideon, By the three hundred men that lapped will I save you, and deliver the Midianites into thy hand; and let all the people go every man unto his place.

units.leftText: So Gideon sent the rest of the Israelites to their tents but kept the three hundred men, who took charge of the provisions and rams’ horns of the others. And the camp of Midian lay below him in the valley. The Sword of Gideon
units.rightText: So the people took victuals in their hand, and their trumpets; and he sent all the men of Israel every man unto his tent, but retained the three hundred men: and the camp of Midian was beneath him in the valley.

units.leftText: That night the LORD said to Gideon, “Get up and go down against the camp, for I have delivered it into your hand.
units.rightText: And it came to pass the same night, that Jehovah said unto him, Arise, get thee down into the camp; for I have delivered it into thy hand.

units.leftText: But if you are afraid to do so, then go down to the camp with your servant Purah
units.rightText: But if thou fear to go down, go thou with Purah thy servant down to the camp:

units.leftText: and listen to what they are saying. Then your hands will be strengthened to attack the camp.” So he went with Purah his servant to the outposts where armed men were guarding the camp.
units.rightText: and thou shalt hear what they say; and afterward shall thy hands be strengthened to go down into the camp. Then went he down with Purah his servant unto the outermost part of the armed men that were in the camp.

units.leftText: Now the Midianites, Amalekites, and all the other people of the east had settled in the valley like a swarm of locusts, and their camels were as countless as the sand on the seashore.
units.rightText: And the Midianites and the Amalekites and all the children of the east lay along in the valley like locusts for multitude; and their camels were without number, as the sand which is upon the sea-shore for multitude.

units.leftText: And as Gideon arrived, a man was telling his friend about a dream. “Behold, I had a dream,” he said, “and I saw a loaf of barley bread come tumbling into the Midianite camp. It struck the tent so hard that the tent overturned and collapsed.”
units.rightText: And when Gideon was come, behold, there was a man telling a dream unto his fellow; and he said, Behold, I dreamed a dream; and, lo, a cake of barley bread tumbled into the camp of Midian, and came unto the tent, and smote it so that it fell, and turned it upside down, so that the tent lay flat.

units.leftText: His friend replied: “This is nothing less than the sword of Gideon son of Joash, the Israelite. God has delivered Midian and the whole camp into his hand.” Gideon Defeats Midian
units.rightText: And his fellow answered and said, This is nothing else save the sword of Gideon the son of Joash, a man of Israel: into his hand God hath delivered Midian, and all the host.

units.leftText: When Gideon heard the dream and its interpretation, he bowed in worship. He returned to the camp of Israel and said, “Get up, for the LORD has delivered the camp of Midian into your hand.”
units.rightText: And it was so, when Gideon heard the telling of the dream, and the interpretation thereof, that he worshipped; and he returned into the camp of Israel, and said, Arise; for Jehovah hath delivered into your hand the host of Midian.

units.leftText: And he divided the three hundred men into three companies and gave each man a ram’s horn in one hand and a large jar in the other, containing a torch.
units.rightText: And he divided the three hundred men into three companies, and he put into the hands of all of them trumpets, and empty pitchers, with torches within the pitchers.
leftNotes: 7:16 Literally and put rams’ horns and empty jars—large jars with torches inside—into the hand of all

units.leftText: “Watch me and do as I do,” Gideon said. “When I come to the outskirts of the camp, do exactly as I do.
units.rightText: And he said unto them, Look on me, and do likewise: and, behold, when I come to the outermost part of the camp, it shall be that, as I do, so shall ye do.

units.leftText: When I and all who are with me blow our horns, then you are also to blow your horns from all around the camp and shout, ‘For the LORD and for Gideon!’”
units.rightText: When I blow the trumpet, I and all that are with me, then blow ye the trumpets also on every side of all the camp, and say, For Jehovah and for Gideon.

units.leftText: Gideon and the hundred men with him reached the outskirts of the camp at the beginning of the middle watch, just after the changing of the guard. They blew their horns and broke the jars that were in their hands.
units.rightText: So Gideon, and the hundred men that were with him, came unto the outermost part of the camp in the beginning of the middle watch, when they had but newly set the watch: and they blew the trumpets, and brake in pieces the pitchers that were in their hands.

units.leftText: The three companies blew their horns and shattered their jars. Holding the torches in their left hands and the horns in their right hands, they shouted, “A sword for the LORD and for Gideon!”
units.rightText: And the three companies blew the trumpets, and brake the pitchers, and held the torches in their left hands, and the trumpets in their right hands wherewith to blow; and they cried, The sword of Jehovah and of Gideon.

units.leftText: Each Israelite took his position around the camp, and the entire Midianite army fled, crying out as they ran.
units.rightText: And they stood every man in his place round about the camp; and all the host ran; and they shouted, and put them to flight.

units.leftText: And when the three hundred rams’ horns sounded, the LORD set all the men in the camp against one another with their swords. The army fled to Beth-shittah toward Zererah as far as the border of Abel-meholah near Tabbath.
units.rightText: And they blew the three hundred trumpets, and Jehovah set every man’s sword against his fellow, and against all the host; and the host fled as far as Beth-shittah toward Zererah, as far as the border of Abel-meholah, by Tabbath.
leftNotes: 7:22 Some Hebrew manuscripts Zeredah

units.leftText: Then the men of Israel were called out from Naphtali, Asher, and all Manasseh, and they pursued the Midianites.
units.rightText: And the men of Israel were gathered together out of Naphtali, and out of Asher, and out of all Manasseh, and pursued after Midian.

units.leftText: Gideon sent messengers throughout the hill country of Ephraim to say, “Come down against the Midianites and seize the waters of the Jordan ahead of them as far as Beth-barah.” So all the men of Ephraim were called out, and they captured the waters of the Jordan as far as Beth-barah.
units.rightText: And Gideon sent messengers throughout all the hill-country of Ephraim, saying, Come down against Midian, and take before them the waters, as far as Beth-barah, even the Jordan. So all the men of Ephraim were gathered together, and took the waters as far as Beth-barah, even the Jordan.

units.leftText: They also captured Oreb and Zeeb, the two princes of Midian; and they killed Oreb at the rock of Oreb and Zeeb at the winepress of Zeeb. So they pursued the Midianites and brought the heads of Oreb and Zeeb to Gideon on the other side of the Jordan.
units.rightText: And they took the two princes of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb; and they slew Oreb at the rock of Oreb, and Zeeb they slew at the winepress of Zeeb, and pursued Midian: and they brought the heads of Oreb and Zeeb to Gideon beyond the Jordan.

units.leftText: Then the men of Ephraim said to Gideon, “Why have you done this to us? Why did you fail to call us when you went to fight against Midian?” And they contended with him violently.
units.rightText: And the men of Ephraim said unto him, Why hast thou served us thus, that thou calledst us not, when thou wentest to fight with Midian? And they did chide with him sharply.

units.leftText: But Gideon answered them, “Now what have I accomplished compared to you? Are not the gleanings of Ephraim better than the grape harvest of Abiezer?
units.rightText: And he said unto them, What have I now done in comparison with you? Is not the gleaning of the grapes of Ephraim better than the vintage of Abiezer?

units.leftText: God has delivered Oreb and Zeeb, the two princes of Midian, into your hand. What was I able to do compared to you?” When he had said this, their anger against him subsided.
units.rightText: God hath delivered into your hand the princes of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb: and what was I able to do in comparison with you? Then their anger was abated toward him, when he had said that.
leftNotes: 8:3 Or their spirit

units.leftText: Then Gideon and his three hundred men came to the Jordan and crossed it, exhausted yet still in pursuit.
units.rightText: And Gideon came to the Jordan, and passed over, he, and the three hundred men that were with him, faint, yet pursuing.

units.leftText: So Gideon said to the men of Succoth, “Please give my troops some bread, for they are exhausted, and I am still pursuing Zebah and Zalmunna, the kings of Midian.”
units.rightText: And he said unto the men of Succoth, Give, I pray you, loaves of bread unto the people that follow me; for they are faint, and I am pursuing after Zebah and Zalmunna, the kings of Midian.

units.leftText: But the leaders of Succoth asked, “Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna already in your possession, that we should give bread to your army?”
units.rightText: And the princes of Succoth said, Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna now in thy hand, that we should give bread unto thine army?

units.leftText: “Very well,” Gideon replied, “when the LORD has delivered Zebah and Zalmunna into my hand, I will tear your flesh with the thorns and briers of the wilderness!”
units.rightText: And Gideon said, Therefore when Jehovah hath delivered Zebah and Zalmunna into my hand, then I will tear your flesh with the thorns of the wilderness and with briers.

units.leftText: From there he went up to Penuel and asked the same from them, but the men of Penuel gave the same response as the men of Succoth.
units.rightText: And he went up thence to Penuel, and spake unto them in like manner; and the men of Penuel answered him as the men of Succoth had answered.
leftNotes: 8:8 Penuel is a variant of Peniel; also in verses 9 and 17; see Genesis 32:30|GEN 32:30*.

units.leftText: So Gideon told the men of Penuel, “When I return in triumph, I will tear down this tower!”
units.rightText: And he spake also unto the men of Penuel, saying, When I come again in peace, I will break down this tower.

units.leftText: Now Zebah and Zalmunna were in Karkor with their army of about fifteen thousand men — all that were left of the armies of the people of the east. A hundred and twenty thousand swordsmen had already fallen.
units.rightText: Now Zebah and Zalmunna were in Karkor, and their hosts with them, about fifteen thousand men, all that were left of all the host of the children of the east; for there fell a hundred and twenty thousand men that drew sword.

units.leftText: And Gideon went up by way of the caravan route east of Nobah and Jogbehah, and he attacked their army, taking them by surprise.
units.rightText: And Gideon went up by the way of them that dwelt in tents on the east of Nobah and Jogbehah, and smote the host; for the host was secure.

units.leftText: When Zebah and Zalmunna fled, Gideon pursued and captured these two kings of Midian, routing their entire army.
units.rightText: And Zebah and Zalmunna fled; and he pursued after them; and he took the two kings of Midian, Zebah and Zalmunna, and discomfited all the host.

units.leftText: After this, Gideon son of Joash returned from the battle along the Ascent of Heres.
units.rightText: And Gideon the son of Joash returned from the battle from the ascent of Heres.

units.leftText: There he captured a young man of Succoth and interrogated him. The young man wrote down for him the names of the seventy-seven leaders and elders of Succoth.
units.rightText: And he caught a young man of the men of Succoth, and inquired of him: and he described for him the princes of Succoth, and the elders thereof, seventy and seven men.

units.leftText: And Gideon went to the men of Succoth and said, “Here are Zebah and Zalmunna, about whom you taunted me, saying, ‘Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna already in your possession, that we should give bread to your weary men?’”
units.rightText: And he came unto the men of Succoth, and said, Behold Zebah and Zalmunna, concerning whom ye did taunt me, saying, Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna now in thy hand, that we should give bread unto thy men that are weary?

units.leftText: Then he took the elders of the city, and using the thorns and briers of the wilderness, he disciplined the men of Succoth.
units.rightText: And he took the elders of the city, and thorns of the wilderness and briers, and with them he taught the men of Succoth.

units.leftText: He also pulled down the tower of Penuel and killed the men of the city.
units.rightText: And he brake down the tower of Penuel, and slew the men of the city.

units.leftText: Next, Gideon asked Zebah and Zalmunna, “What kind of men did you kill at Tabor?” “Men like you,” they answered, “each one resembling the son of a king.”
units.rightText: Then said he unto Zebah and Zalmunna, What manner of men were they whom ye slew at Tabor? And they answered, As thou art, so were they; each one resembled the children of a king.

units.leftText: “They were my brothers,” Gideon replied, “the sons of my mother! As surely as the LORD lives, if you had let them live, I would not kill you.”
units.rightText: And he said, They were my brethren, the sons of my mother: as Jehovah liveth, if ye had saved them alive, I would not slay you.

units.leftText: So he said to Jether, his firstborn, “Get up and kill them.” But the young man did not draw his sword; he was fearful because he was still a youth.
units.rightText: And he said unto Jether his first-born, Up, and slay them. But the youth drew not his sword; for he feared, because he was yet a youth.

units.leftText: Then Zebah and Zalmunna said, “Get up and kill us yourself, for as the man is, so is his strength.” So Gideon got up and killed Zebah and Zalmunna, and he took the crescent ornaments from the necks of their camels. Gideon’s Ephod
units.rightText: Then Zebah and Zalmunna said, Rise thou, and fall upon us; for as the man is, so is his strength. And Gideon arose, and slew Zebah and Zalmunna, and took the crescents that were on their camels’ necks.

units.leftText: Then the Israelites said to Gideon, “Rule over us — you and your son and grandson — for you have saved us from the hand of Midian.”
units.rightText: Then the men of Israel said unto Gideon, Rule thou over us, both thou, and thy son, and thy son’s son also; for thou hast saved us out of the hand of Midian.

units.leftText: But Gideon replied, “I will not rule over you, nor will my son. The LORD shall rule over you.”
