units.rightText: And Gideon said unto them, I will not rule over you, neither shall my son rule over you: Jehovah shall rule over you.

units.leftText: Then he added, “Let me make a request of you, that each of you give me an earring from his plunder.” (For the enemies had gold earrings because they were Ishmaelites.)
units.rightText: And Gideon said unto them, I would make a request of you, that ye would give me every man the ear-rings of his spoil. (For they had golden ear-rings, because they were Ishmaelites.)

units.leftText: “We will give them gladly,” they replied.
units.rightText: And they answered, We will willingly give them. And they spread a garment, and did cast therein every man the ear-rings of his spoil.

units.leftText: The weight of the gold earrings he had requested was 1 ,700 shekels, in addition to the crescent ornaments, the pendants, the purple garments of the kings of Midian, and the chains from the necks of their camels.
units.rightText: And the weight of the golden ear-rings that he requested was a thousand and seven hundred shekels of gold; besides the crescents, and the pendants, and the purple raiment that was on the kings of Midian, and besides the chains that were about their camels’ necks.
leftNotes: 8:26 1,700 shekels is approximately 42.7 pounds or 19.4 kilograms.

units.leftText: From all this Gideon made an ephod, which he placed in Ophrah, his hometown. But soon all Israel prostituted themselves by worshiping it there, and it became a snare to Gideon and his household. Forty Years of Peace
units.rightText: And Gideon made an ephod thereof, and put it in his city, even in Ophrah: and all Israel played the harlot after it there; and it became a snare unto Gideon, and to his house.

units.leftText: In this way Midian was subdued before the Israelites and did not raise its head again. So the land had rest for forty years in the days of Gideon,
units.rightText: So Midian was subdued before the children of Israel, and they lifted up their heads no more. And the land had rest forty years in the days of Gideon.

units.leftText: and he — Jerubbaal son of Joash — returned home and settled down.
units.rightText: And Jerubbaal the son of Joash went and dwelt in his own house.
leftNotes: 8:29 Jerubbaal is another name for Gideon and probably means let Baal contend; also in verse 35; see Judges 6:32|JDG 6:32*.

units.leftText: Gideon had seventy sons of his own, since he had many wives.
units.rightText: And Gideon had threescore and ten sons of his body begotten; for he had many wives.
leftNotes: 8:30 Hebrew who came from his own loins

units.leftText: His concubine, who dwelt in Shechem, also bore him a son, and he named him Abimelech. Gideon’s Death
units.rightText: And his concubine that was in Shechem, she also bare him a son, and he called his name Abimelech.

units.leftText: Later, Gideon son of Joash died at a ripe old age and was buried in the tomb of his father Joash in Ophrah of the Abiezrites.
units.rightText: And Gideon the son of Joash died in a good old age, and was buried in the sepulchre of Joash his father, in Ophrah of the Abiezrites.

units.leftText: And as soon as Gideon was dead, the Israelites turned and prostituted themselves with the Baals, and they set up Baal-berith as their god.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, as soon as Gideon was dead, that the children of Israel turned again, and played the harlot after the Baalim, and made Baal-berith their god.

units.leftText: The Israelites failed to remember the LORD their God who had delivered them from the hands of all their enemies on every side.
units.rightText: And the children of Israel remembered not Jehovah their God, who had delivered them out of the hand of all their enemies on every side;

units.leftText: They did not show kindness to the house of Jerubbaal (that is, Gideon) for all the good things he had done for Israel.
units.rightText: neither showed they kindness to the house of Jerubbaal, who is Gideon, according to all the goodness which he had showed unto Israel.

units.leftText: Now Abimelech son of Jerubbaal went to his mother’s brothers at Shechem and said to them and to all the clan of his mother,
units.rightText: And Abimelech the son of Jerubbaal went to Shechem unto his mother’s brethren, and spake with them, and with all the family of the house of his mother’s father, saying,
leftNotes: 9:1 Jerubbaal is another name for Gideon and probably means let Baal contend; here and throughout this chapter; see Judges 6:32|JDG 6:32*.

units.leftText: “Please ask all the leaders of Shechem, ‘Is it better for you that seventy men, all the sons of Jerubbaal, rule over you, or just one man?’ Remember that I am your own flesh and blood.”
units.rightText: Speak, I pray you, in the ears of all the men of Shechem, Whether is better for you, that all the sons of Jerubbaal, who are threescore and ten persons, rule over you, or that one rule over you? remember also that I am your bone and your flesh.

units.leftText: And when his mother’s brothers spoke all these words about him in the presence of all the leaders of Shechem, their hearts were inclined to follow Abimelech, for they said, “He is our brother.”
units.rightText: And his mother’s brethren spake of him in the ears of all the men of Shechem all these words: and their hearts inclined to follow Abimelech; for they said, He is our brother.

units.leftText: So they gave him seventy shekels of silver from the temple of Baal-berith, with which Abimelech hired some worthless and reckless men to follow him.
units.rightText: And they gave him threescore and ten pieces of silver out of the house of Baal-berith, wherewith Abimelech hired vain and light fellows, who followed him.
leftNotes: 9:4 70 shekels is approximately 1.76 pounds or 797.8 grams of silver.

units.leftText: He went to his father’s house in Ophrah, and on one stone murdered his seventy brothers, the sons of Jerubbaal. But Jotham, the youngest son of Jerubbaal, survived, because he hid himself.
units.rightText: And he went unto his father’s house at Ophrah, and slew his brethren the sons of Jerubbaal, being threescore and ten persons, upon one stone: but Jotham the youngest son of Jerubbaal was left; for he hid himself.

units.leftText: Then all the leaders of Shechem and Beth-millo gathered beside the oak at the pillar in Shechem and proceeded to make Abimelech their king. Jotham’s Parable
units.rightText: And all the men of Shechem assembled themselves together, and all the house of Millo, and went and made Abimelech king, by the oak of the pillar that was in Shechem.
leftNotes: 9:6 Or terebinth or great tree

units.leftText: When this was reported to Jotham, he climbed to the top of Mount Gerizim, raised his voice, and cried out: “Listen to me, O leaders of Shechem, and may God listen to you.
units.rightText: And when they told it to Jotham, he went and stood on the top of mount Gerizim, and lifted up his voice, and cried, and said unto them, Hearken unto me, ye men of Shechem, that God may hearken unto you.

units.leftText: One day the trees set out to anoint a king for themselves. They said to the olive tree, ‘Reign over us.’
units.rightText: The trees went forth on a time to anoint a king over them; and they said unto the olive-tree, Reign thou over us.

units.leftText: But the olive tree replied, ‘Should I stop giving my oil that honors both God and man, to hold sway over the trees?’
units.rightText: But the olive-tree said unto them, Should I leave my fatness, wherewith by me they honor God and man, and go to wave to and fro over the trees?

units.leftText: Then the trees said to the fig tree, ‘Come and reign over us.’
units.rightText: And the trees said to the fig-tree, Come thou, and reign over us.

units.leftText: But the fig tree replied, ‘Should I stop giving my sweetness and my good fruit, to hold sway over the trees?’
units.rightText: But the fig-tree said unto them, Should I leave my sweetness, and my good fruit, and go to wave to and fro over the trees?

units.leftText: Then the trees said to the grapevine, ‘Come and reign over us.’
units.rightText: And the trees said unto the vine, Come thou, and reign over us.

units.leftText: But the grapevine replied, ‘Should I stop giving my wine that cheers both God and man, to hold sway over the trees?’
units.rightText: And the vine said unto them, Should I leave my new wine, which cheereth God and man, and go to wave to and fro over the trees?

units.leftText: Finally all the trees said to the thornbush, ‘Come and reign over us.’
units.rightText: Then said all the trees unto the bramble, Come thou, and reign over us.

units.leftText: But the thornbush replied, ‘If you really are anointing me as king over you, come and find refuge in my shade. But if not, may fire come out of the thornbush and consume the cedars of Lebanon.’
units.rightText: And the bramble said unto the trees, If in truth ye anoint me king over you, then come and take refuge in my shade; and if not, let fire come out of the bramble, and devour the cedars of Lebanon.

units.leftText: Now if you have acted faithfully and honestly in making Abimelech king, if you have done well by Jerubbaal and his family, and if you have done to him as he deserves—
units.rightText: Now therefore, if ye have dealt truly and uprightly, in that ye have made Abimelech king, and if ye have dealt well with Jerubbaal and his house, and have done unto him according to the deserving of his hands

units.leftText: for my father fought for you and risked his life to deliver you from the hand of Midian,
units.rightText: (for my father fought for you, and adventured his life, and delivered you out of the hand of Midian:

units.leftText: but you have risen up against my father’s house this day and killed his seventy sons on a single stone, and you have made Abimelech, the son of his maidservant, king over the leaders of Shechem because he is your brother —
units.rightText: and ye are risen up against my father’s house this day, and have slain his sons, threescore and ten persons, upon one stone, and have made Abimelech, the son of his maid-servant, king over the men of Shechem, because he is your brother);

units.leftText: if you have acted faithfully and honestly toward Jerubbaal and his house this day, then may you rejoice in Abimelech, and he in you.
units.rightText: if ye then have dealt truly and uprightly with Jerubbaal and with his house this day, then rejoice ye in Abimelech, and let him also rejoice in you:

units.leftText: But if not, may fire come from Abimelech and consume the leaders of Shechem and Beth-millo, and may fire come from the leaders of Shechem and Beth-millo and consume Abimelech.”
units.rightText: but if not, let fire come out from Abimelech, and devour the men of Shechem, and the house of Millo; and let fire come out from the men of Shechem, and from the house of Millo, and devour Abimelech.

units.leftText: Then Jotham ran away, escaping to Beer, and he lived there for fear of his brother Abimelech. Gaal Conspires with the Shechemites
units.rightText: And Jotham ran away, and fled, and went to Beer, and dwelt there, for fear of Abimelech his brother.

units.leftText: After Abimelech had reigned over Israel for three years,
units.rightText: And Abimelech was prince over Israel three years.

units.leftText: God sent a spirit of animosity between Abimelech and the leaders of Shechem and caused them to treat Abimelech deceitfully,
units.rightText: And God sent an evil spirit between Abimelech and the men of Shechem; and the men of Shechem dealt treacherously with Abimelech:
leftNotes: 9:23 Or a harmful spirit

units.leftText: in order that the crime against the seventy sons of Jerubbaal might come to justice and their blood be avenged on their brother Abimelech and on the leaders of Shechem, who had helped him murder his brothers.
units.rightText: that the violence done to the threescore and ten sons of Jerubbaal might come, and that their blood might be laid upon Abimelech their brother, who slew them, and upon the men of Shechem, who strengthened his hands to slay his brethren.

units.leftText: The leaders of Shechem set up an ambush against Abimelech on the hilltops, and they robbed all who passed by them on the road. So this was reported to Abimelech.
units.rightText: And the men of Shechem set liers-in-wait for him on the tops of the mountains, and they robbed all that came along that way by them: and it was told Abimelech.

units.leftText: Meanwhile, Gaal son of Ebed came with his brothers and crossed into Shechem, and the leaders of Shechem put their confidence in him.
units.rightText: And Gaal the son of Ebed came with his brethren, and went over to Shechem; and the men of Shechem put their trust in him.

units.leftText: And after they had gone out into the fields, gathered grapes from their vineyards, and trodden them, they held a festival and went into the house of their god; and as they ate and drank, they cursed Abimelech.
units.rightText: And they went out into the field, and gathered their vineyards, and trod the grapes, and held festival, and went into the house of their god, and did eat and drink, and cursed Abimelech.

units.leftText: Then Gaal son of Ebed said, “Who is Abimelech, and who is Shechem, that we should serve him? Is he not the son of Jerubbaal, and is not Zebul his officer? You are to serve the men of Hamor, the father of Shechem. Why should we serve Abimelech?
units.rightText: And Gaal the son of Ebed said, Who is Abimelech, and who is Shechem, that we should serve him? is not he the son of Jerubbaal? and Zebul his officer? serve ye the men of Hamor the father of Shechem: but why should we serve him?

units.leftText: If only this people were under my authority, I would remove Abimelech; I would say to him, ‘Muster your army and come out!’” The Fall of Shechem
units.rightText: And would that this people were under my hand! then would I remove Abimelech. And he said to Abimelech, Increase thine army, and come out.
leftNotes: 9:29 LXX; Hebrew I would remove Abimelech.” And he said to him, “Muster your army and come out!”

units.leftText: When Zebul the governor of the city heard the words of Gaal son of Ebed, he burned with anger.
units.rightText: And when Zebul the ruler of the city heard the words of Gaal the son of Ebed, his anger was kindled.

units.leftText: So he covertly sent messengers to Abimelech to say, “Look, Gaal son of Ebed and his brothers have come to Shechem and are stirring up the city against you.
units.rightText: And he sent messengers unto Abimelech craftily, saying, Behold, Gaal the son of Ebed and his brethren are come to Shechem; and, behold, they constrain the city to take part against thee.
leftNotes: 9:31 Or he sent messengers to Abimelech in Arumah; see verse 41.
9:31 Or besieging or closing up

units.leftText: Now then, tonight you and the people with you are to come and lie in wait in the fields.
units.rightText: Now therefore, up by night, thou and the people that are with thee, and lie in wait in the field:

units.leftText: And in the morning at sunrise, get up and advance against the city. When Gaal and his men come out against you, do to them whatever you are able.”
units.rightText: and it shall be, that in the morning, as soon as the sun is up, thou shalt rise early, and rush upon the city; and, behold, when he and the people that are with him come out against thee, then mayest thou do to them as thou shalt find occasion.

units.leftText: So Abimelech and all his troops set out by night and lay in wait against Shechem in four companies.
units.rightText: And Abimelech rose up, and all the people that were with him, by night, and they laid wait against Shechem in four companies.

units.leftText: Now Gaal son of Ebed went out and stood at the entrance of the city gate just as Abimelech and his men came out from their hiding places.
units.rightText: And Gaal the son of Ebed went out, and stood in the entrance of the gate of the city: and Abimelech rose up, and the people that were with him, from the ambushment.

units.leftText: When Gaal saw the people, he said to Zebul, “Look, people are coming down from the mountains!” But Zebul replied, “The shadows of the mountains look like men to you.”
units.rightText: And when Gaal saw the people, he said to Zebul, Behold, there come people down from the tops of the mountains. And Zebul said unto him, Thou seest the shadow of the mountains as if they were men.

units.leftText: Then Gaal spoke up again, “Look, people are coming down from the center of the land, and one company is coming by way of the Diviners’ Oak. ”
units.rightText: And Gaal spake again and said, See, there come people down by the middle of the land, and one company cometh by the way of the oak of Meonenim.
leftNotes: 9:37 Literally the navel of the earth
9:37 Or the Diviners’ Terebinth or the diviners’ tree

units.leftText: “Where is your gloating now?” Zebul replied. “You said, ‘Who is Abimelech that we should serve him?’ Are these not the people you ridiculed? Go out now and fight them!”
units.rightText: Then said Zebul unto him, Where is now thy mouth, that thou saidst, Who is Abimelech, that we should serve him? is not this the people that thou hast despised? go out now, I pray, and fight with them.

units.leftText: So Gaal went out before the leaders of Shechem and fought against Abimelech,
units.rightText: And Gaal went out before the men of Shechem, and fought with Abimelech.

units.leftText: but Abimelech pursued him, and Gaal fled before him. And many Shechemites fell wounded all the way to the entrance of the gate.
units.rightText: And Abimelech chased him, and he fled before him, and there fell many wounded, even unto the entrance of the gate.

units.leftText: Abimelech stayed in Arumah, and Zebul drove Gaal and his brothers out of Shechem.
units.rightText: And Abimelech dwelt at Arumah: and Zebul drove out Gaal and his brethren, that they should not dwell in Shechem.

units.leftText: The next day the people of Shechem went out into the fields, and this was reported to Abimelech.
units.rightText: And it came to pass on the morrow, that the people went out into the field; and they told Abimelech.

units.leftText: So he took his men, divided them into three companies, and lay in wait in the fields. When he saw the people coming out of the city, he rose up against them and attacked them.
units.rightText: And he took the people, and divided them into three companies, and laid wait in the field; and he looked, and, behold, the people came forth out of the city; and he rose up against them, and smote them.

units.leftText: Then Abimelech and the companies with him rushed forward and took their stand at the entrance of the city gate. The other two companies rushed against all who were in the fields and struck them down.
units.rightText: And Abimelech, and the companies that were with him, rushed forward, and stood in the entrance of the gate of the city: and the two companies rushed upon all that were in the field, and smote them.

units.leftText: And all that day Abimelech fought against the city until he had captured it and killed its people. Then he demolished the city and sowed it with salt.
units.rightText: And Abimelech fought against the city all that day; and he took the city, and slew the people that were therein: and he beat down the city, and sowed it with salt.

units.leftText: On hearing of this, all the leaders in the tower of Shechem entered the inner chamber of the temple of El-berith.
units.rightText: And when all the men of the tower of Shechem heard thereof, they entered into the stronghold of the house of Elberith.
leftNotes: 9:46 El-berith was another name for Baal-berith; see verse 4.

units.leftText: And when Abimelech was told that all the leaders in the tower of Shechem were gathered there,
units.rightText: And it was told Abimelech that all the men of the tower of Shechem were gathered together.

units.leftText: he and all his men went up to Mount Zalmon. Abimelech took his axe in his hand and cut a branch from the trees, which he lifted to his shoulder, saying to his men, “Hurry and do what you have seen me do.”
units.rightText: And Abimelech gat him up to mount Zalmon, he and all the people that were with him; and Abimelech took an axe in his hand, and cut down a bough from the trees, and took it up, and laid it on his shoulder: and he said unto the people that were with him, What ye have seen me do, make haste, and do as I have done.

units.leftText: So each man also cut his own branch and followed Abimelech. Then they piled the branches against the inner chamber and set it on fire above them, killing everyone in the tower of Shechem, about a thousand men and women. Abimelech’s Punishment
units.rightText: And all the people likewise cut down every man his bough, and followed Abimelech, and put them to the stronghold, and set the stronghold on fire upon them; so that all the men of the tower of Shechem died also, about a thousand men and women.

units.leftText: Then Abimelech went to Thebez, encamped against it, and captured it.
units.rightText: Then went Abimelech to Thebez, and encamped against Thebez, and took it.

units.leftText: But there was a strong tower inside the city, and all the men, women, and leaders of the city fled there. They locked themselves in and went up to the roof of the tower.
units.rightText: But there was a strong tower within the city, and thither fled all the men and women, and all they of the city, and shut themselves in, and gat them up to the roof of the tower.

units.leftText: When Abimelech came to attack the tower, he approached its entrance to set it on fire.
units.rightText: And Abimelech came unto the tower, and fought against it, and drew near unto the door of the tower to burn it with fire.

units.leftText: But a woman dropped an upper millstone on Abimelech’s head, crushing his skull.
units.rightText: And a certain woman cast an upper millstone upon Abimelech’s head, and brake his skull.

units.leftText: He quickly called his armor-bearer, saying, “Draw your sword and kill me, lest they say of me, ‘A woman killed him.’”
units.rightText: Then he called hastily unto the young man his armorbearer, and said unto him, Draw thy sword, and kill me, that men say not of me, A woman slew him. And his young man thrust him through, and he died.

units.leftText: And when the Israelites saw that Abimelech was dead, they all went home.
units.rightText: And when the men of Israel saw that Abimelech was dead, they departed every man unto his place.

units.leftText: In this way God repaid the wickedness that Abimelech had done to his father in murdering his seventy brothers.
units.rightText: Thus God requited the wickedness of Abimelech, which he did unto his father, in slaying his seventy brethren;

units.leftText: And God also brought all the wickedness of the men of Shechem back upon their own heads. So the curse of Jotham son of Jerubbaal came upon them.
units.rightText: and all the wickedness of the men of Shechem did God requite upon their heads: and upon them came the curse of Jotham the son of Jerubbaal.

units.leftText: After the time of Abimelech, a man of Issachar, Tola son of Puah, the son of Dodo, rose up to save Israel. He lived in Shamir, in the hill country of Ephraim.
units.rightText: And after Abimelech there arose to save Israel Tola the son of Puah, the son of Dodo, a man of Issachar; and he dwelt in Shamir in the hill-country of Ephraim.

units.leftText: Tola judged Israel twenty-three years, and when he died, he was buried in Shamir. Jair
units.rightText: And he judged Israel twenty and three years, and died, and was buried in Shamir.
leftNotes: 10:2 Or governed or led; here and throughout the book of Judges

units.leftText: Tola was followed by Jair the Gileadite, who judged Israel twenty-two years.
units.rightText: And after him arose Jair, the Gileadite; and he judged Israel twenty and two years.

units.leftText: He had thirty sons who rode on thirty donkeys. And they had thirty towns in the land of Gilead, which to this day are called Havvoth-jair.
units.rightText: And he had thirty sons that rode on thirty ass colts, and they had thirty cities, which are called Havvoth-jair unto this day, which are in the land of Gilead.
leftNotes: 10:4 Or the villages of Jair

units.leftText: When Jair died, he was buried in Kamon. Oppression by the Philistines and Ammonites
units.rightText: And Jair died, and was buried in Kamon.

units.leftText: And again the Israelites did evil in the sight of the LORD. They served the Baals, the Ashtoreths, the gods of Aram, Sidon, and Moab, and the gods of the Ammonites and Philistines. Thus they forsook the LORD and did not serve Him.
units.rightText: And the children of Israel again did that which was evil in the sight of Jehovah, and served the Baalim, and the Ashtaroth, and the gods of Syria, and the gods of Sidon, and the gods of Moab, and the gods of the children of Ammon, and the gods of the Philistines; and they forsook Jehovah, and served him not.

units.leftText: So the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and He sold them into the hands of the Philistines and Ammonites,
units.rightText: And the anger of Jehovah was kindled against Israel, and he sold them into the hand of the Philistines, and into the hand of the children of Ammon.

units.leftText: who that very year harassed and oppressed the Israelites, and they did so for eighteen years to all the Israelites on the other side of the Jordan in Gilead, the land of the Amorites.
units.rightText: And they vexed and oppressed the children of Israel that year: eighteen years oppressed they all the children of Israel that were beyond the Jordan in the land of the Amorites, which is in Gilead.

units.leftText: The Ammonites also crossed the Jordan to fight against Judah, Benjamin, and the house of Ephraim, and Israel was in deep distress.
units.rightText: And the children of Ammon passed over the Jordan to fight also against Judah, and against Benjamin, and against the house of Ephraim; so that Israel was sore distressed.

units.leftText: Then the Israelites cried out to the LORD, saying, “We have sinned against You, for we have indeed forsaken our God and served the Baals.”
units.rightText: And the children of Israel cried unto Jehovah, saying, We have sinned against thee, even because we have forsaken our God, and have served the Baalim.

units.leftText: The LORD replied, “When the Egyptians, Amorites, Ammonites, Philistines,
units.rightText: And Jehovah said unto the children of Israel, Did not I save you from the Egyptians, and from the Amorites, from the children of Ammon, and from the Philistines?

units.leftText: Sidonians, Amalekites, and Maonites oppressed you and you cried out to Me, did I not save you from their hands?
units.rightText: The Sidonians also, and the Amalekites, and the Maonites, did oppress you; and ye cried unto me, and I saved you out of their hand.
leftNotes: 10:12 Hebrew; some LXX manuscripts Midianites

units.leftText: But you have forsaken Me and served other gods, so I will no longer save you.
units.rightText: Yet ye have forsaken me, and served other gods: wherefore I will save you no more.

units.leftText: Go and cry out to the gods you have chosen. Let them save you in your time of trouble.”
units.rightText: Go and cry unto the gods which ye have chosen; let them save you in the time of your distress.

units.leftText: “We have sinned,” the Israelites said to the LORD. “Deal with us as You see fit; but please deliver us today!”
units.rightText: And the children of Israel said unto Jehovah, We have sinned: do thou unto us whatsoever seemeth good unto thee; only deliver us, we pray thee, this day.

units.leftText: So they put away the foreign gods from among them and served the LORD, and He could no longer bear the misery of Israel.
units.rightText: And they put away the foreign gods from among them, and served Jehovah; and his soul was grieved for the misery of Israel.

units.leftText: Then the Ammonites were called to arms and camped in Gilead, and the Israelites assembled and camped at Mizpah.
units.rightText: Then the children of Ammon were gathered together, and encamped in Gilead. And the children of Israel assembled themselves together, and encamped in Mizpah.

units.leftText: And the rulers of Gilead said to one another, “Whoever will launch the attack against the Ammonites will be the head of all who live in Gilead.”
units.rightText: And the people, the princes of Gilead, said one to another, What man is he that will begin to fight against the children of Ammon? he shall be head over all the inhabitants of Gilead.

units.leftText: Now Jephthah the Gileadite was a mighty man of valor; he was the son of a prostitute, and Gilead was his father.
units.rightText: Now Jephthah the Gileadite was a mighty man of valor, and he was the son of a harlot: and Gilead begat Jephthah.

units.leftText: And Gilead’s wife bore him sons who grew up, drove Jephthah out, and said to him, “You shall have no inheritance in our father’s house, because you are the son of another woman.”
units.rightText: And Gilead’s wife bare him sons; and when his wife’s sons grew up, they drove out Jephthah, and said unto him, Thou shalt not inherit in our father’s house; for thou art the son of another woman.

units.leftText: So Jephthah fled from his brothers and settled in the land of Tob, where worthless men gathered around him and traveled with him.
units.rightText: Then Jephthah fled from his brethren, and dwelt in the land of Tob: and there were gathered vain fellows to Jephthah, and they went out with him.

units.leftText: Some time later, when the Ammonites fought against Israel
units.rightText: And it came to pass after a while, that the children of Ammon made war against Israel.

units.leftText: and made war with them, the elders of Gilead went to get Jephthah from the land of Tob.
units.rightText: And it was so, that, when the children of Ammon made war against Israel, the elders of Gilead went to fetch Jephthah out of the land of Tob;

units.leftText: “Come,” they said, “be our commander, so that we can fight against the Ammonites.”
units.rightText: and they said unto Jephthah, Come and be our chief, that we may fight with the children of Ammon.

units.leftText: Jephthah replied to the elders of Gilead, “Did you not hate me and expel me from my father’s house? Why then have you come to me now, when you are in distress?”
units.rightText: And Jephthah said unto the elders of Gilead, Did not ye hate me, and drive me out of my father’s house? and why are ye come unto me now when ye are in distress?

units.leftText: They answered Jephthah, “This is why we now turn to you, that you may go with us, fight the Ammonites, and become leader over all of us who live in Gilead.”
units.rightText: And the elders of Gilead said unto Jephthah, Therefore are we turned again to thee now, that thou mayest go with us, and fight with the children of Ammon; and thou shalt be our head over all the inhabitants of Gilead.

units.leftText: But Jephthah asked them, “If you take me back to fight the Ammonites and the LORD gives them to me, will I really be your leader?”
units.rightText: And Jephthah said unto the elders of Gilead, If ye bring me home again to fight with the children of Ammon, and Jehovah deliver them before me, shall I be your head?

units.leftText: And the elders of Gilead said to Jephthah, “The LORD is our witness if we do not do as you say.”
units.rightText: And the elders of Gilead said unto Jephthah, Jehovah shall be witness between us; surely according to thy word so will we do.

units.leftText: So Jephthah went with the elders of Gilead, and the people made him their leader and commander. And Jephthah repeated all his terms in the presence of the LORD at Mizpah.
units.rightText: Then Jephthah went with the elders of Gilead, and the people made him head and chief over them: and Jephthah spake all his words before Jehovah in Mizpah.

units.leftText: Then Jephthah sent messengers to the king of the Ammonites, saying, “What do you have against me that you have come to fight against my land?”
units.rightText: And Jephthah sent messengers unto the king of the children of Ammon, saying, What hast thou to do with me, that thou art come unto me to fight against my land?

units.leftText: The king of the Ammonites answered Jephthah’s messengers, “When Israel came up out of Egypt, they seized my land, from the Arnon to the Jabbok and all the way to the Jordan. Now, therefore, restore it peaceably.”
units.rightText: And the king of the children of Ammon answered unto the messengers of Jephthah, Because Israel took away my land, when he came up out of Egypt, from the Arnon even unto the Jabbok, and unto the Jordan: now therefore restore those lands again peaceably.

units.leftText: Jephthah again sent messengers to the king of the Ammonites
units.rightText: And Jephthah sent messengers again unto the king of the children of Ammon;

units.leftText: to tell him, “This is what Jephthah says: Israel did not take away the land of Moab or of the Ammonites.
units.rightText: and he said unto him, Thus saith Jephthah: Israel took not away the land of Moab, nor the land of the children of Ammon;

units.leftText: But when Israel came up out of Egypt, they traveled through the wilderness to the Red Sea and came to Kadesh.
units.rightText: but when they came up from Egypt, and Israel went through the wilderness unto the Red Sea, and came to Kadesh;
leftNotes: 11:16 Or the Sea of Reeds

units.leftText: Then Israel sent messengers to the king of Edom, saying, ‘Please let us pass through your land,’ but the king of Edom would not listen. They also sent messengers to the king of Moab, but he would not consent. So Israel stayed in Kadesh.
units.rightText: then Israel sent messengers unto the king of Edom, saying, Let me, I pray thee, pass through thy land; but the king of Edom hearkened not. And in like manner he sent unto the king of Moab; but he would not: and Israel abode in Kadesh.

units.leftText: Then Israel traveled through the wilderness and bypassed the lands of Edom and Moab. They came to the east side of the land of Moab and camped on the other side of the Arnon. But they did not enter the territory of Moab, since the Arnon was its border.
units.rightText: Then they went through the wilderness, and went around the land of Edom, and the land of Moab, and came by the east side of the land of Moab, and they encamped on the other side of the Arnon; but they came not within the border of Moab, for the Arnon was the border of Moab.

units.leftText: And Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, who ruled in Heshbon, and said to him, ‘Please let us pass through your land into our own place.’
units.rightText: And Israel sent messengers unto Sihon king of the Amorites, the king of Heshbon; and Israel said unto him, Let us pass, we pray thee, through thy land unto my place.

units.leftText: But Sihon would not trust Israel to pass through his territory. So he gathered all his people, encamped in Jahaz, and fought with Israel.
units.rightText: But Sihon trusted not Israel to pass through his border; but Sihon gathered all his people together, and encamped in Jahaz, and fought against Israel.

units.leftText: Then the LORD, the God of Israel, delivered Sihon and all his people into the hand of Israel, who defeated them. So Israel took possession of all the land of the Amorites who inhabited that country,
units.rightText: And Jehovah, the God of Israel, delivered Sihon and all his people into the hand of Israel, and they smote them: so Israel possessed all the land of the Amorites, the inhabitants of that country.

units.leftText: seizing all the land from the Arnon to the Jabbok and from the wilderness to the Jordan.
units.rightText: And they possessed all the border of the Amorites, from the Arnon even unto the Jabbok, and from the wilderness even unto the Jordan.

units.leftText: Now since the LORD, the God of Israel, has driven out the Amorites from before His people Israel, should you now possess it?
units.rightText: So now Jehovah, the God of Israel, hath dispossessed the Amorites from before his people Israel, and shouldest thou possess them?

units.leftText: Do you not possess whatever your god Chemosh grants you? So also, we possess whatever the LORD our God has granted us.
units.rightText: Wilt not thou possess that which Chemosh thy god giveth thee to possess? So whomsoever Jehovah our God hath dispossessed from before us, them will we possess.

units.leftText: Are you now so much better than Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab? Did he ever contend with Israel or fight against them?
units.rightText: And now art thou anything better than Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab? did he ever strive against Israel, or did he ever fight against them?

units.leftText: For three hundred years Israel has lived in Heshbon, Aroer, and their villages, as well as all the cities along the banks of the Arnon. Why did you not take them back during that time?
units.rightText: While Israel dwelt in Heshbon and its towns, and in Aroer and its towns, and in all the cities that are along by the side of the Arnon, three hundred years; wherefore did ye not recover them within that time?

units.leftText: I have not sinned against you, but you have done me wrong by waging war against me. May the LORD, the Judge, decide today between the Israelites and the Ammonites.”
units.rightText: I therefore have not sinned against thee, but thou doest me wrong to war against me: Jehovah, the Judge, be judge this day between the children of Israel and the children of Ammon.

units.leftText: But the king of the Ammonites paid no heed to the message Jephthah sent him. Jephthah’s Tragic Vow
units.rightText: Howbeit the king of the children of Ammon hearkened not unto the words of Jephthah which he sent him.

units.leftText: Then the Spirit of the LORD came upon Jephthah, and he passed through Gilead and Manasseh, then through Mizpah of Gilead. And from there he advanced against the Ammonites.
units.rightText: Then the Spirit of Jehovah came upon Jephthah, and he passed over Gilead and Manasseh, and passed over Mizpeh of Gilead, and from Mizpeh of Gilead he passed over unto the children of Ammon.

units.leftText: Jephthah made this vow to the LORD: “If indeed You will deliver the Ammonites into my hand,
units.rightText: And Jephthah vowed a vow unto Jehovah, and said, If thou wilt indeed deliver the children of Ammon into my hand,

units.leftText: then whatever comes out the door of my house to greet me on my triumphant return from the Ammonites will belong to the LORD, and I will offer it up as a burnt offering.”
units.rightText: then it shall be, that whatsoever cometh forth from the doors of my house to meet me, when I return in peace from the children of Ammon, it shall be Jehovah’s, and I will offer it up for a burnt-offering.

units.leftText: So Jephthah crossed over to the Ammonites to fight against them, and the LORD delivered them into his hand.
units.rightText: So Jephthah passed over unto the children of Ammon to fight against them; and Jehovah delivered them into his hand.

units.leftText: With a great blow he devastated twenty cities from Aroer to the vicinity of Minnith, as far as Abel-keramim. So the Ammonites were subdued before the Israelites.
units.rightText: And he smote them from Aroer until thou come to Minnith, even twenty cities, and unto Abel-cheramim, with a very great slaughter. So the children of Ammon were subdued before the children of Israel.

units.leftText: And when Jephthah returned home to Mizpah, there was his daughter coming out to meet him with tambourines and dancing! She was his only child; he had no son or daughter besides her.
units.rightText: And Jephthah came to Mizpah unto his house; and, behold, his daughter came out to meet him with timbrels and with dances: and she was his only child; besides her he had neither son nor daughter.

units.leftText: As soon as Jephthah saw her, he tore his clothes and said, “No! Not my daughter! You have brought me to my knees! You have brought great misery upon me, for I have given my word to the LORD and cannot take it back.”
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when he saw her, that he rent his clothes, and said, Alas, my daughter! thou hast brought me very low, and thou art one of them that trouble me; for I have opened my mouth unto Jehovah, and I cannot go back.

units.leftText: “My father,” she replied, “you have given your word to the LORD. Do to me as you have said, for the LORD has avenged you of your enemies, the Ammonites.”
units.rightText: And she said unto him, My father, thou hast opened thy mouth unto Jehovah; do unto me according to that which hath proceeded out of thy mouth, forasmuch as Jehovah hath taken vengeance for thee on thine enemies, even on the children of Ammon.

units.leftText: She also said to her father, “Let me do this one thing: Let me wander for two months through the mountains with my friends and mourn my virginity.”
units.rightText: And she said unto her father, Let this thing be done for me: let me alone two months, that I may depart and go down upon the mountains, and bewail my virginity, I and my companions.

units.leftText: “Go,” he said. And he sent her away for two months.
units.rightText: And he said, Go. And he sent her away for two months: and she departed, she and her companions, and bewailed her virginity upon the mountains.

units.leftText: After two months, she returned to her father, and he did to her as he had vowed. And she had never had relations with a man.
units.rightText: And it came to pass at the end of two months, that she returned unto her father, who did with her according to his vow which he had vowed: and she knew not man. And it was a custom in Israel,

units.leftText: that each year the young women of Israel go out for four days to lament the daughter of Jephthah the Gileadite.
units.rightText: that the daughters of Israel went yearly to celebrate the daughter of Jephthah the Gileadite four days in a year.

units.leftText: Then the men of Ephraim assembled and crossed the Jordan to Zaphon. They said to Jephthah, “Why have you crossed over to fight the Ammonites without calling us to go with you? We will burn your house down with you inside!”
units.rightText: And the men of Ephraim were gathered together, and passed northward; and they said unto Jephthah, Wherefore passedst thou over to fight against the children of Ammon, and didst not call us to go with thee? we will burn thy house upon thee with fire.

units.leftText: But Jephthah replied, “My people and I had a serious conflict with the Ammonites, and when I called, you did not save me out of their hands.
units.rightText: And Jephthah said unto them, I and my people were at great strife with the children of Ammon; and when I called you, ye saved me not out of their hand.

units.leftText: When I saw that you would not save me, I risked my life and crossed over to the Ammonites, and the LORD delivered them into my hand. Why then have you come today to fight against me?”
units.rightText: And when I saw that ye saved me not, I put my life in my hand, and passed over against the children of Ammon, and Jehovah delivered them into my hand: wherefore then are ye come up unto me this day, to fight against me?

units.leftText: Jephthah then gathered all the men of Gilead and fought against Ephraim. And the men of Gilead struck them down because the Ephraimites had said, “You Gileadites are fugitives in Ephraim, living in the territories of Ephraim and Manasseh.”
units.rightText: Then Jephthah gathered together all the men of Gilead, and fought with Ephraim; and the men of Gilead smote Ephraim, because they said, Ye are fugitives of Ephraim, ye Gileadites, in the midst of Ephraim, and in the midst of Manasseh.

units.leftText: The Gileadites captured the fords of the Jordan leading to Ephraim, and whenever a fugitive from Ephraim would say, “Let me cross over,” the Gileadites would ask him, “Are you an Ephraimite?”
units.rightText: And the Gileadites took the fords of the Jordan against the Ephraimites. And it was so, that, when any of the fugitives of Ephraim said, Let me go over, the men of Gilead said unto him, Art thou an Ephraimite? If he said, Nay;

units.leftText: they told him, “Please say Shibboleth.” If he said, “Sibboleth,” because he could not pronounce it correctly, they seized him and killed him at the fords of the Jordan. So at that time 42,000 Ephraimites were killed.
units.rightText: then said they unto him, Say now Shibboleth; and he said Sibboleth; for he could not frame to pronounce it right: then they laid hold on him, and slew him at the fords of the Jordan. And there fell at that time of Ephraim forty and two thousand.

units.leftText: Jephthah judged Israel six years, and when he died, he was buried in one of the cities of Gilead. Ibzan, Elon, and Abdon
units.rightText: And Jephthah judged Israel six years. Then died Jephthah the Gileadite, and was buried in one of the cities of Gilead.
leftNotes: 12:7 LXX in his city in Gilead

units.leftText: After Jephthah, Ibzan of Bethlehem judged Israel.
units.rightText: And after him Ibzan of Beth-lehem judged Israel.

units.leftText: He had thirty sons, as well as thirty daughters whom he gave in marriage to men outside his clan; and for his sons he brought back thirty wives from elsewhere. Ibzan judged Israel seven years.
units.rightText: And he had thirty sons; and thirty daughters he sent abroad, and thirty daughters he brought in from abroad for his sons. And he judged Israel seven years.

units.leftText: Then Ibzan died, and he was buried in Bethlehem.
units.rightText: And Ibzan died, and was buried at Beth-lehem.

units.leftText: After Ibzan, Elon the Zebulunite judged Israel ten years.
units.rightText: And after him Elon the Zebulunite judged Israel; and he judged Israel ten years.

units.leftText: Then Elon the Zebulunite died, and he was buried in Aijalon in the land of Zebulun.
units.rightText: And Elon the Zebulunite died, and was buried in Aijalon in the land of Zebulun.

units.leftText: After Elon, Abdon son of Hillel, from Pirathon, judged Israel.
units.rightText: And after him Abdon the son of Hillel the Pirathonite judged Israel.

units.leftText: He had forty sons and thirty grandsons, who rode on seventy donkeys. And he judged Israel eight years.
units.rightText: And he had forty sons and thirty sons’ sons, that rode on threescore and ten ass colts: and he judged Israel eight years.

units.leftText: Then Abdon son of Hillel, from Pirathon, died, and he was buried at Pirathon in Ephraim, in the hill country of the Amalekites.
units.rightText: And Abdon the son of Hillel the Pirathonite died, and was buried in Pirathon in the land of Ephraim, in the hill-country of the Amalekites.

units.leftText: Again the Israelites did evil in the sight of the LORD, so He delivered them into the hand of the Philistines for forty years.
units.rightText: And the children of Israel again did that which was evil in the sight of Jehovah; and Jehovah delivered them into the hand of the Philistines forty years.

units.leftText: Now there was a man from Zorah named Manoah, from the clan of the Danites, whose wife was barren and had no children.
units.rightText: And there was a certain man of Zorah, of the family of the Danites, whose name was Manoah; and his wife was barren, and bare not.

units.leftText: The angel of the LORD appeared to the woman and said to her, “It is true that you are barren and have no children; but you will conceive and give birth to a son.
units.rightText: And the angel of Jehovah appeared unto the woman, and said unto her, Behold now, thou art barren, and bearest not; but thou shalt conceive, and bear a son.
leftNotes: 13:3 Or Angel; here and throughout chapter 13; corresponding pronouns may also be capitalized.

units.leftText: Now please be careful not to drink wine or strong drink, and not to eat anything unclean.
units.rightText: Now therefore beware, I pray thee, and drink no wine nor strong drink, and eat not any unclean thing:

units.leftText: For behold, you will conceive and give birth to a son. And no razor shall touch his head, because the boy will be a Nazirite to God from the womb, and he will begin the deliverance of Israel from the hand of the Philistines.”
units.rightText: for, lo, thou shalt conceive, and bear a son; and no razor shall come upon his head; for the child shall be a Nazirite unto God from the womb: and he shall begin to save Israel out of the hand of the Philistines.
leftNotes: 13:5 Or set apart

units.leftText: So the woman went and told her husband, “A man of God came to me. His appearance was like the angel of God, exceedingly awesome. I did not ask him where he came from, and he did not tell me his name.
units.rightText: Then the woman came and told her husband, saying, A man of God came unto me, and his countenance was like the countenance of the angel of God, very terrible; and I asked him not whence he was, neither told he me his name:

units.leftText: But he said to me, ‘Behold, you will conceive and give birth to a son. Now, therefore, do not drink wine or strong drink, and do not eat anything unclean, because the boy will be a Nazirite to God from the womb until the day of his death.’”
units.rightText: but he said unto me, Behold, thou shalt conceive, and bear a son; and now drink no wine nor strong drink, and eat not any unclean thing; for the child shall be a Nazirite unto God from the womb to the day of his death.

units.leftText: Then Manoah prayed to the LORD, “Please, O Lord, let the man of God You sent us come to us again to teach us how to raise the boy who is to be born.”
units.rightText: Then Manoah entreated Jehovah, and said, Oh, Lord, I pray thee, let the man of God whom thou didst send come again unto us, and teach us what we shall do unto the child that shall be born.

units.leftText: And God listened to the voice of Manoah, and the angel of God returned to the woman as she was sitting in the field; but her husband Manoah was not with her.
units.rightText: And God hearkened to the voice of Manoah; and the angel of God came again unto the woman as she sat in the field: but Manoah her husband was not with her.

units.leftText: The woman ran quickly to tell her husband, “Behold, the man who came to me the other day has reappeared!”
units.rightText: And the woman made haste, and ran, and told her husband, and said unto him, Behold, the man hath appeared unto me, that came unto me the other day.

units.leftText: So Manoah got up and followed his wife. When he came to the man, he asked, “Are you the man who spoke to my wife?” “I am, ” he said.
units.rightText: And Manoah arose, and went after his wife, and came to the man, and said unto him, Art thou the man that spakest unto the woman? And he said, I am.

units.leftText: Then Manoah asked, “When your words come to pass, what will be the boy’s rule of life and mission?”
units.rightText: And Manoah said, Now let thy words come to pass: what shall be the ordering of the child, and how shall we do unto him?

units.leftText: So the angel of the LORD answered Manoah, “Your wife is to do everything I told her.
units.rightText: And the angel of Jehovah said unto Manoah, Of all that I said unto the woman let her beware.

units.leftText: She must not eat anything that comes from the vine, nor drink any wine or strong drink, nor eat anything unclean. She must do everything I have commanded her.”
units.rightText: She may not eat of anything that cometh of the vine, neither let her drink wine or strong drink, nor eat any unclean thing; all that I commanded her let her observe.

units.leftText: “Please stay here,” Manoah said to the angel of the LORD, “and we will prepare a young goat for you.”
units.rightText: And Manoah said unto the angel of Jehovah, I pray thee, let us detain thee, that we may make ready a kid for thee.

units.leftText: And the angel of the LORD replied, “Even if I stay, I will not eat your food. But if you prepare a burnt offering, offer it to the LORD.” For Manoah did not know that it was the angel of the LORD.
units.rightText: And the angel of Jehovah said unto Manoah, Though thou detain me, I will not eat of thy bread; and if thou wilt make ready a burnt-offering, thou must offer it unto Jehovah. For Manoah knew not that he was the angel of Jehovah.

units.leftText: Then Manoah said to the angel of the LORD, “What is your name, so that we may honor you when your word comes to pass?”
units.rightText: And Manoah said unto the angel of Jehovah, What is thy name, that, when thy words come to pass, we may do thee honor?

units.leftText: “Why do you ask my name,” said the angel of the LORD, “since it is beyond comprehension?”
units.rightText: And the angel of Jehovah said unto him, Wherefore askest thou after my name, seeing it is wonderful?

units.leftText: Then Manoah took a young goat and a grain offering and offered them on a rock to the LORD. And as Manoah and his wife looked on, the LORD did a marvelous thing.
units.rightText: So Manoah took the kid with the meal-offering, and offered it upon the rock unto Jehovah: and the angel did wondrously, and Manoah and his wife looked on.

units.leftText: When the flame went up from the altar to the sky, the angel of the LORD ascended in the flame.
units.rightText: For it came to pass, when the flame went up toward heaven from off the altar, that the angel of Jehovah ascended in the flame of the altar: and Manoah and his wife looked on; and they fell on their faces to the ground.

units.leftText: And when the angel of the LORD did not appear again to Manoah and his wife, Manoah realized that it had been the angel of the LORD.
units.rightText: But the angel of Jehovah did no more appear to Manoah or to his wife. Then Manoah knew that he was the angel of Jehovah.

units.leftText: “We are going to die,” he said to his wife, “for we have seen God!”
units.rightText: And Manoah said unto his wife, We shall surely die, because we have seen God.

units.leftText: But his wife replied, “If the LORD had intended to kill us, He would not have accepted the burnt offering and the grain offering from our hands, nor would He have shown us all these things or spoken to us this way.”
units.rightText: But his wife said unto him, If Jehovah were pleased to kill us, he would not have received a burnt-offering and a meal-offering at our hand, neither would he have showed us all these things, nor would at this time have told such things as these.

units.leftText: So the woman gave birth to a son and named him Samson. The boy grew, and the LORD blessed him.
units.rightText: And the woman bare a son, and called his name Samson: and the child grew, and Jehovah blessed him.

units.leftText: And the Spirit of the LORD began to stir him at Mahaneh-dan, between Zorah and Eshtaol.
units.rightText: And the Spirit of Jehovah began to move him in Mahaneh-dan, between Zorah and Eshtaol.
leftNotes: 13:25 Mahaneh-dan means camp of Dan.

units.leftText: One day Samson went down to Timnah, where he saw a young Philistine woman.
units.rightText: And Samson went down to Timnah, and saw a woman in Timnah of the daughters of the Philistines.

units.leftText: So he returned and told his father and mother, “I have seen a daughter of the Philistines in Timnah. Now get her for me as a wife.”
units.rightText: And he came up, and told his father and his mother, and said, I have seen a woman in Timnah of the daughters of the Philistines: now therefore get her for me to wife.

units.leftText: But his father and mother replied, “Can’t you find a young woman among your relatives or among any of our people? Must you go to the uncircumcised Philistines to get a wife?”
units.rightText: Then his father and his mother said unto him, Is there never a woman among the daughters of thy brethren, or among all my people, that thou goest to take a wife of the uncircumcised Philistines? And Samson said unto his father, Get her for me; for she pleaseth me well.

units.leftText: (Now his father and mother did not know this was from the LORD, who was seeking an occasion to move against the Philistines; for at that time the Philistines were ruling over Israel.)
units.rightText: But his father and his mother knew not that it was of Jehovah; for he sought an occasion against the Philistines. Now at that time the Philistines had rule over Israel.

units.leftText: Then Samson went down to Timnah with his father and mother and came to the vineyards of Timnah. Suddenly a young lion came roaring at him,
units.rightText: Then went Samson down, and his father and his mother, to Timnah, and came to the vineyards of Timnah: and, behold, a young lion roared against him.

units.leftText: and the Spirit of the LORD came powerfully upon him, and he tore the lion apart with his bare hands as one would tear a young goat. But he did not tell his father or mother what he had done.
units.rightText: And the Spirit of Jehovah came mightily upon him, and he rent him as he would have rent a kid; and he had nothing in his hand: but he told not his father or his mother what he had done.

units.leftText: Then Samson continued on his way down and spoke to the woman, because she was pleasing to his eyes. Samson’s Riddle
units.rightText: And he went down, and talked with the woman, and she pleased Samson well.

units.leftText: When Samson returned later to take her, he left the road to see the lion’s carcass, and in it was a swarm of bees, along with their honey.
units.rightText: And after a while he returned to take her; and he turned aside to see the carcass of the lion: and, behold, there was a swarm of bees in the body of the lion, and honey.

units.leftText: So he scooped some honey into his hands and ate it as he went along. And when he returned to his father and mother, he gave some to them and they ate it. But he did not tell them that he had taken the honey from the lion’s carcass.
units.rightText: And he took it into his hands, and went on, eating as he went; and he came to his father and mother, and gave unto them, and they did eat: but he told them not that he had taken the honey out of the body of the lion.

units.leftText: Then his father went to visit the woman, and Samson prepared a feast there, as was customary for the bridegroom.
units.rightText: And his father went down unto the woman: and Samson made there a feast; for so used the young men to do.

units.leftText: And when the Philistines saw him, they selected thirty men to accompany him.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when they saw him, that they brought thirty companions to be with him.
leftNotes: 14:11 Or when the bride’s parents saw him; literally when they saw him

units.leftText: “Let me tell you a riddle,” Samson said to them. “If you can solve it for me within the seven days of the feast, I will give you thirty linen garments and thirty sets of clothes.
units.rightText: And Samson said unto them, Let me now put forth a riddle unto you: if ye can declare it unto me within the seven days of the feast, and find it out, then I will give you thirty linen garments and thirty changes of raiment;

units.leftText: But if you cannot solve it, you must give me thirty linen garments and thirty sets of clothes.” “Tell us your riddle,” they replied. “Let us hear it.”
units.rightText: but if ye cannot declare it unto me, then shall ye give me thirty linen garments and thirty changes of raiment. And they said unto him, Put forth thy riddle, that we may hear it.

units.leftText: So he said to them: “Out of the eater came something to eat, and out of the strong came something sweet.”
units.rightText: And he said unto them, Out of the eater came forth food, And out of the strong came forth sweetness. And they could not in three days declare the riddle.

units.leftText: So on the fourth day they said to Samson’s wife, “Entice your husband to explain the riddle to us, or we will burn you and your father’s household to death. Did you invite us here to rob us?”
units.rightText: And it came to pass on the seventh day, that they said unto Samson’s wife, Entice thy husband, that he may declare unto us the riddle, lest we burn thee and thy father’s house with fire: have ye called us to impoverish us? is it not so?
leftNotes: 14:15 LXX and Syriac; Hebrew seventh

units.leftText: Then Samson’s wife came to him, weeping, and said, “You hate me! You do not really love me! You have posed to my people a riddle, but have not explained it to me.” “Look,” he said, “I have not even explained it to my father or mother, so why should I explain it to you?”
units.rightText: And Samson’s wife wept before him, and said, Thou dost but hate me, and lovest me not: thou hast put forth a riddle unto the children of my people, and hast not told it me. And he said unto her, Behold, I have not told it my father nor my mother, and shall I tell thee?

units.leftText: She wept the whole seven days of the feast, and finally on the seventh day, because she had pressed him so much, he told her the answer. And in turn she explained the riddle to her people.
units.rightText: And she wept before him the seven days, while their feast lasted: and it came to pass on the seventh day, that he told her, because she pressed him sore; and she told the riddle to the children of her people.

units.leftText: Before sunset on the seventh day, the men of the city said to Samson: “What is sweeter than honey? And what is stronger than a lion?” So he said to them: “If you had not plowed with my heifer, you would not have solved my riddle!”
units.rightText: And the men of the city said unto him on the seventh day before the sun went down, What is sweeter than honey? and what is stronger than a lion? And he said unto them, If ye had not plowed with my heifer, Ye had not found out my riddle.

units.leftText: Then the Spirit of the LORD came mightily upon him, and he went down to Ashkelon, killed thirty of their men, took their apparel, and gave their clothes to those who had solved the riddle. And burning with anger, Samson returned to his father’s house,
units.rightText: And the Spirit of Jehovah came mightily upon him, and he went down to Ashkelon, and smote thirty men of them, and took their spoil, and gave the changes of raiment unto them that declared the riddle. And his anger was kindled, and he went up to his father’s house.

units.leftText: and his wife was given to one of the men who had accompanied him.
units.rightText: But Samson’s wife was given to his companion, whom he had used as his friend.

units.leftText: Later on, at the time of the wheat harvest, Samson took a young goat and went to visit his wife. “I want to go to my wife in her room,” he said. But her father would not let him enter.
units.rightText: But it came to pass after a while, in the time of wheat harvest, that Samson visited his wife with a kid; and he said, I will go in to my wife into the chamber. But her father would not suffer him to go in.

units.leftText: “I was sure that you thoroughly hated her,” said her father, “so I gave her to one of the men who accompanied you. Is not her younger sister more beautiful than she? Please take her instead.”
units.rightText: And her father said, I verily thought that thou hadst utterly hated her; therefore I gave her to thy companion: is not her younger sister fairer than she? take her, I pray thee, instead of her.

units.leftText: Samson said to them, “This time I will be blameless in doing harm to the Philistines.”
units.rightText: And Samson said unto them, This time shall I be blameless in regard of the Philistines, when I do them a mischief.

units.leftText: Then Samson went out and caught three hundred foxes. And he took torches, turned the foxes tail-to-tail, and fastened a torch between each pair of tails.
units.rightText: And Samson went and caught three hundred foxes, and took firebrands, and turned tail to tail, and put a firebrand in the midst between every two tails.

units.leftText: Then he lit the torches and released the foxes into the standing grain of the Philistines, burning up the piles of grain and the standing grain, as well as the vineyards and olive groves.
units.rightText: And when he had set the brands on fire, he let them go into the standing grain of the Philistines, and burnt up both the shocks and the standing grain, and also the oliveyards.

units.leftText: “Who did this?” the Philistines demanded. “It was Samson, the son-in-law of the Timnite,” they were told. “For his wife was given to his companion.” So the Philistines went up and burned her and her father to death.
units.rightText: Then the Philistines said, Who hath done this? And they said, Samson, the son-in-law of the Timnite, because he hath taken his wife, and given her to his companion. And the Philistines came up, and burnt her and her father with fire.

units.leftText: And Samson told them, “Because you have done this, I will not rest until I have taken vengeance upon you.”
units.rightText: And Samson said unto them, If ye do after this manner, surely I will be avenged of you, and after that I will cease.

units.leftText: And he struck them ruthlessly with a great slaughter, and then went down and stayed in the cave at the rock of Etam.
units.rightText: And he smote them hip and thigh with a great slaughter: and he went down and dwelt in the cleft of the rock of Etam.
leftNotes: 15:8 Literally he struck them hip and thigh

units.leftText: Then the Philistines went up, camped in Judah, and deployed themselves near the town of Lehi.
units.rightText: Then the Philistines went up, and encamped in Judah, and spread themselves in Lehi.
leftNotes: 15:9 Literally and spread out in Lehi

units.leftText: “Why have you attacked us?” said the men of Judah. The Philistines replied, “We have come to arrest Samson and pay him back for what he has done to us.”
units.rightText: And the men of Judah said, Why are ye come up against us? And they said, To bind Samson are we come up, to do to him as he hath done to us.

units.leftText: In response, three thousand men of Judah went to the cave at the rock of Etam, and they asked Samson, “Do you not realize that the Philistines rule over us? What have you done to us?” “I have done to them what they did to me,” he replied.
units.rightText: Then three thousand men of Judah went down to the cleft of the rock of Etam, and said to Samson, Knowest thou not that the Philistines are rulers over us? what then is this that thou hast done unto us? And he said unto them, As they did unto me, so have I done unto them.

units.leftText: But they said to him, “We have come down to arrest you and hand you over to the Philistines.” Samson replied, “Swear to me that you will not kill me yourselves.”
units.rightText: And they said unto him, We are come down to bind thee, that we may deliver thee into the hand of the Philistines. And Samson said unto them, Swear unto me, that ye will not fall upon me yourselves.

units.leftText: “No,” they answered, “we will not kill you, but we will tie you up securely and hand you over to them.” So they bound him with two new ropes and led him up from the rock.
units.rightText: And they spake unto him, saying, No; but we will bind thee fast, and deliver thee into their hand: but surely we will not kill thee. And they bound him with two new ropes, and brought him up from the rock.

units.leftText: When Samson arrived in Lehi, the Philistines came out shouting against him. And the Spirit of the LORD came mightily upon him. The ropes on his arms became like burnt flax, and the bonds broke loose from his hands.
units.rightText: When he came unto Lehi, the Philistines shouted as they met him: and the Spirit of Jehovah came mightily upon him, and the ropes that were upon his arms became as flax that was burnt with fire, and his bands dropped from off his hands.

units.leftText: He found the fresh jawbone of a donkey, reached out his hand and took it, and struck down a thousand men.
units.rightText: And he found a fresh jawbone of an ass, and put forth his hand, and took it, and smote a thousand men therewith.

units.leftText: Then Samson said: “With the jawbone of a donkey I have piled them into heaps. With the jawbone of a donkey I have slain a thousand men.”
units.rightText: And Samson said, With the jawbone of an ass, heaps upon heaps, With the jawbone of an ass have I smitten a thousand men.
leftNotes: 15:16 Or I have made them into donkeys

units.leftText: And when Samson had finished speaking, he cast the jawbone from his hand; and he named that place Ramath-lehi.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when he had made an end of speaking, that he cast away the jawbone out of his hand; and that place was called Ramath-lehi.
leftNotes: 15:17 Ramath-lehi means the hill of the jawbone.

units.leftText: And being very thirsty, Samson cried out to the LORD, “You have accomplished this great deliverance through Your servant. Must I now die of thirst and fall into the hands of the uncircumcised?”
units.rightText: And he was sore athirst, and called on Jehovah, and said, Thou hast given this great deliverance by the hand of thy servant; and now shall I die for thirst, and fall into the hand of the uncircumcised.

units.leftText: So God opened up the hollow place in Lehi, and water came out of it. When Samson drank, his strength returned, and he was revived. That is why he named it En-hakkore, and it remains in Lehi to this day.
units.rightText: But God clave the hollow place that is in Lehi, and there came water thereout; and when he had drunk, his spirit came again, and he revived: wherefore the name thereof was called En-hakkore, which is in Lehi, unto this day.
leftNotes: 15:19 En-hakkore means the spring of him who calls.

units.leftText: And Samson judged Israel for twenty years in the days of the Philistines.
units.rightText: And he judged Israel in the days of the Philistines twenty years.

units.leftText: One day Samson went to Gaza, where he saw a prostitute and went in to spend the night with her.
units.rightText: And Samson went to Gaza, and saw there a harlot, and went in unto her.

units.leftText: When the Gazites heard that Samson was there, they surrounded that place and lay in wait for him all night at the city gate. They were quiet throughout the night, saying, “Let us wait until dawn; then we will kill him.”
units.rightText: And it was told the Gazites, saying, Samson is come hither. And they compassed him in, and laid wait for him all night in the gate of the city, and were quiet all the night, saying, Let be till morning light, then we will kill him.

units.leftText: But Samson lay there only until midnight, when he got up, took hold of the doors of the city gate and both gateposts, and pulled them out, bar and all. Then he put them on his shoulders and took them to the top of the mountain overlooking Hebron. Samson and Delilah
units.rightText: And Samson lay till midnight, and arose at midnight, and laid hold of the doors of the gate of the city, and the two posts, and plucked them up, bar and all, and put them upon his shoulders, and carried them up to the top of the mountain that is before Hebron.

units.leftText: Some time later, Samson fell in love with a woman in the Valley of Sorek, whose name was Delilah.
units.rightText: And it came to pass afterward, that he loved a woman in the valley of Sorek, whose name was Delilah.

units.leftText: The lords of the Philistines went to her and said, “Entice him and find out the source of his great strength and how we can overpower him to tie him up and subdue him. Then each one of us will give you eleven hundred shekels of silver. ”
units.rightText: And the lords of the Philistines came up unto her, and said unto her, Entice him, and see wherein his great strength lieth, and by what means we may prevail against him, that we may bind him to afflict him: and we will give thee every one of us eleven hundred pieces of silver.
leftNotes: 16:5 1,100 shekels is approximately 27.6 pounds or 12.5 kilograms of silver.

units.leftText: So Delilah said to Samson, “Please tell me the source of your great strength and how you can be tied up and subdued.”
units.rightText: And Delilah said to Samson, Tell me, I pray thee, wherein thy great strength lieth, and wherewith thou mightest be bound to afflict thee.

units.leftText: Samson told her, “If they tie me up with seven fresh bowstrings that have not been dried, I will become as weak as any other man.”
units.rightText: And Samson said unto her, If they bind me with seven green withes that were never dried, then shall I become weak, and be as another man.

units.leftText: So the lords of the Philistines brought her seven fresh bowstrings that had not been dried, and she tied him up with them.
units.rightText: Then the lords of the Philistines brought up to her seven green withes which had not been dried, and she bound him with them.

units.leftText: While the men were hidden in her room, she called out, “Samson, the Philistines are here!” But he snapped the bowstrings like a strand of yarn seared by a flame. So the source of his strength remained unknown.
units.rightText: Now she had liers-in-wait abiding in the inner chamber. And she said unto him, The Philistines are upon thee, Samson. And he brake the withes, as a string of tow is broken when it toucheth the fire. So his strength was not known.

units.leftText: Then Delilah said to Samson, “You have mocked me and lied to me! Now please tell me how you can be tied up.”
units.rightText: And Delilah said unto Samson, Behold, thou hast mocked me, and told me lies: now tell me, I pray thee, wherewith thou mightest be bound.

units.leftText: He replied, “If they tie me up with new ropes that have never been used, I will become as weak as any other man.”
units.rightText: And he said unto her, If they only bind me with new ropes wherewith no work hath been done, then shall I become weak, and be as another man.

units.leftText: So Delilah took new ropes, tied him up with them, and called out, “Samson, the Philistines are here!” But while the men were hidden in her room, he snapped the ropes off his arms like they were threads.
units.rightText: So Delilah took new ropes, and bound him therewith, and said unto him, The Philistines are upon thee, Samson. And the liers-in-wait were abiding in the inner chamber. And he brake them off his arms like a thread.

units.leftText: Then Delilah said to Samson, “You have mocked me and lied to me all along! Tell me how you can be tied up.” He told her, “If you weave the seven braids of my head into the web of a loom and tighten it with a pin, I will become as weak as any other man. ”
units.rightText: And Delilah said unto Samson, Hitherto thou hast mocked me, and told me lies: tell me wherewith thou mightest be bound. And he said unto her, If thou weavest the seven locks of my head with the web.
leftNotes: 16:13 See LXX and Vulgate; Hebrew does not include and tighten it with a pin, I will become as weak as any other man.

units.leftText: So while he slept, Delilah took the seven braids of his hair and wove them into the web. Then she tightened [it] with a pin and called to him, “Samson, the Philistines are here!” But he awoke from his sleep and pulled out the pin with the loom and the web. Delilah Learns the Secret
units.rightText: And she fastened it with the pin, and said unto him, The Philistines are upon thee, Samson. And he awaked out of his sleep, and plucked away the pin of the beam, and the web.
leftNotes: 16:14 See LXX and Vulgate; Hebrew does not include So while he slept, Delilah took the seven braids of his hair and wove them into the web.

units.leftText: “How can you say, ‘I love you,’” she asked, “when your heart is not with me? This is the third time you have mocked me and failed to reveal to me the source of your great strength!”
units.rightText: And she said unto him, How canst thou say, I love thee, when thy heart is not with me? thou hast mocked me these three times, and hast not told me wherein thy great strength lieth.

units.leftText: Finally, after she had pressed him daily with her words and pleaded until he was sick to death,
units.rightText: And it came to pass, when she pressed him daily with her words, and urged him, that his soul was vexed unto death.

units.leftText: Samson told her all that was in his heart: “My hair has never been cut, because I have been a Nazirite to God from my mother’s womb. If I am shaved, my strength will leave me, and I will become as weak as any other man.”
units.rightText: And he told her all his heart, and said unto her, There hath not come a razor upon my head; for I have been a Nazirite unto God from my mother’s womb: if I be shaven, then my strength will go from me, and I shall become weak, and be like any other man.

units.leftText: When Delilah realized that he had revealed to her all that was in his heart, she sent this message to the lords of the Philistines: “Come up once more, for he has revealed to me all that is in his heart.” Then the lords of the Philistines came to her, bringing the money in their hands.
units.rightText: And when Delilah saw that he had told her all his heart, she sent and called for the lords of the Philistines, saying, Come up this once, for he hath told me all his heart. Then the lords of the Philistines came up unto her, and brought the money in their hand.

units.leftText: And having lulled him to sleep on her lap, she called a man to shave off the seven braids of his head. In this way she began to subdue him, and his strength left him.
units.rightText: And she made him sleep upon her knees; and she called for a man, and shaved off the seven locks of his head; and she began to afflict him, and his strength went from him.
leftNotes: 16:19 Hebrew; some LXX manuscripts he began to grow weak

units.leftText: Then she called out, “Samson, the Philistines are here!” When Samson awoke from his sleep, he thought, “I will escape as I did before and shake myself free.” But he did not know that the LORD had departed from him.
units.rightText: And she said, The Philistines are upon thee, Samson. And he awoke out of his sleep, and said, I will go out as at other times, and shake myself free. But he knew not that Jehovah was departed from him.

units.leftText: Then the Philistines seized him, gouged out his eyes, and brought him down to Gaza, where he was bound with bronze shackles and forced to grind grain in the prison.
units.rightText: And the Philistines laid hold on him, and put out his eyes; and they brought him down to Gaza, and bound him with fetters of brass; and he did grind in the prison-house.

units.leftText: However, the hair of his head began to grow back after it had been shaved. Samson’s Vengeance and Death
units.rightText: Howbeit the hair of his head began to grow again after he was shaven.

units.leftText: Now the lords of the Philistines gathered together to offer a great sacrifice to their god Dagon. They rejoiced and said, “Our god has delivered Samson our enemy into our hands.”
units.rightText: And the lords of the Philistines gathered them together to offer a great sacrifice unto Dagon their god, and to rejoice; for they said, Our god hath delivered Samson our enemy into our hand.

units.leftText: And when the people saw him, they praised their god, saying: “Our god has delivered into our hands our enemy who destroyed our land and multiplied our dead.”
units.rightText: And when the people saw him, they praised their god; for they said, Our god hath delivered into our hand our enemy, and the destroyer of our country, who hath slain many of us.
